items.q: What is AssurePro?
items.a: AssurePro is the practice management platform within AssureOne. It helps accounting firms manage their day-to-day operations from a centralized system, including firm setup, team access, client relationships, documents, engagement workflows, engagement letters, time and billing, communications, reporting, templates, and integrations.
more: AssurePro also provides the shared client and firm context used across other AssureOne products enabled for your organization. By keeping operational information connected to a single client record, teams can move seamlessly between practice management and service delivery without recreating client information or maintaining disconnected records across multiple systems.

items.q: Is AssurePro the firm's practice-management system or a bookkeeping system?
items.a: AssurePro is the firm's practice management system. It manages the operational relationship with clients, including onboarding, document requests, workflows, engagement letters, time tracking, billing, communications, and reporting.
more: Bookkeeping work itself is performed in AssureBooks, when that product is enabled for the firm.

For example, AssurePro can be used to create a bookkeeping engagement, assign tasks, request source documents, track time, communicate with the client, and invoice for the work. The underlying accounting records, transactions, and books are managed in AssureBooks.

When AssureBooks is enabled, firm users can access it through the AssureOne product switcher, allowing them to move between practice management and bookkeeping while maintaining the relevant client context.

items.q: How do I find existing information quickly?
items.a: Use the global search in AssurePro to quickly find information that already exists in the system. You can search for clients, documents, or tasks by name and open the relevant record directly from the search results.
steps: Select the Search field.
Enter the name of the client, document, or task you are looking for.
Review the matching results.
Select the relevant result to open the corresponding client record, document, or task.

items.q: How do I create a new record quickly?
items.a: Use the + New menu in the top-right corner of AssurePro to create common records from anywhere in the application. Depending on your access, you can quickly create a Client, Task, Message, Invoice, Document Request, or Engagement Letter.
more: Selecting an option opens the corresponding creation form, where you can enter the required information and complete the action.

For example, selecting Invoice opens the invoice builder, where you can choose the client, set issue and due dates, add line items, apply discounts or taxes, enter notes, preview the invoice, and either save it as a draft or create and send it.
steps: Select + New in the application header.
Choose the record you want to create: Client, Task, Message, Invoice, Document Request, or Engagement Letter.
Complete the required fields in the form, confirming the relevant client, recipients, or other details.
Select the appropriate completion action, such as Save, Create, Save as draft, or Create & send, depending on the record type.

items.q: Where do firm users sign in?
items.a: Firm users sign in to the internal AssurePro workspace using the access link provided by their firm administrator. A new firm user opens the invitation sent to their work email, verifies the address, and sets a password to activate the account. Client users follow a separate process: they sign in through the firm's client portal or the AssureOne mobile app, on iOS or Android.
more: If a firm user cannot activate the account, first confirm the correct email address was used and ask them to open the most recent invitation. Administrators can review, resend, or cancel a pending invitation under Team & Roles > Invitations.

items.q: How do I get help or report an issue in AssurePro?
items.a: AssureOne provides direct email support, in-product issue reporting, and implementation assistance.
steps: Email support@assureone.ai when you need help from the AssureOne support team, describing the feature, access issue, or workflow involved.

Use Report a bug in the application header to report a product issue from the screen where it occurred, describing what you were doing, what you expected, what actually happened, and the affected area; attach a screenshot when it helps, with no unnecessary sensitive or confidential information.
For configuration, onboarding, or data-migration questions, contact the firm's assigned AssureOne implementation team, since the answer may depend on the firm's plan and rollout.

items.q: Can administrators review recent activity across the firm?
items.a: Yes. Administrators can use the Recent Activity section on the Overview dashboard to review recent user and system activity across the firm.
more: Each activity entry shows the action performed, the related user or record, and when the activity occurred. Depending on the activity captured by AssurePro, this may include events such as a team invitation being sent or accepted, a client signing in to the client portal, a client or contact record being updated, and other supported user or system actions.
Recent Activity is designed to provide administrators with quick visibility into day-to-day activity across the firm.

items.q: What is on the AssurePro Overview?
items.a: The Overview is AssurePro's main operating dashboard. It gives firm users a consolidated view of important activity, priorities, and performance across the practice.
more: The Overview includes an AI-generated daily briefing along with summaries for areas such as clients, engagements, team workload, deadlines, workflow bottlenecks, invoices, tasks, and review work.
You can select a widget, record, or summary item to open the related client, engagement, task, invoice, or report and review the underlying details.

items.q: Can the Overview dashboard be customized?
items.a: Yes. You can customize the Overview dashboard to show the information that is most relevant to your role and day-to-day responsibilities.
more: Select Edit layout to choose which available widgets appear on the dashboard and arrange them in your preferred order. Save the layout when you are finished.
For example, a partner may prioritize financial performance and workflow bottlenecks, while a manager may prefer to focus on engagements, review work, upcoming deadlines, and team capacity.
Your customized layout is saved for your user account. Select Reset layout at any time to restore the standard dashboard arrangement.

items.q: How do I build a custom report?
items.a: You can build a custom dashboard from Reports > Templates by selecting the report widgets that match the information or management question you want to track.
more: After selecting one or more widgets, you can arrange the dashboard layout, adjust widget sizing where available, and save the dashboard for personal use or share it with other firm users who have report access.
steps: Open Reports and select Templates.
Search for a report widget or filter the available widgets by category.
Select the widgets you want to include in the dashboard.
Review the selected widgets. They are initially added in the order in which you selected them.
Drag the widgets into your preferred order. Adjust the widget width and, where available, its height.
Select Save dashboard.
Enter a dashboard name and, optionally, a description.
Choose whether to Share with the firm.
Save the dashboard.
If you share the dashboard with the firm, it becomes available to users who have the required report access. If you do not share it, the dashboard remains available for your own use.

items.q: How do I share or manage a custom dashboard?
items.a: When saving a custom dashboard, enable Share with the firm to make it available to other firm users who have report access.
more: Shared dashboards can be managed using options such as Edit widgets to change the dashboard content or layout, Rename to update the dashboard name, Duplicate to my dashboards to create a personal copy that you can modify independently, Make private to remove the dashboard from firm-wide access without deleting it, and Delete to permanently remove the dashboard.

If you want to experiment with a shared or starter dashboard, use Duplicate to my dashboards first — this lets you make changes without affecting the original. A good practice is to name the dashboard based on the management question or area it is designed to track, update the widgets to match that purpose, and enable Share with the firm only when the dashboard is ready for broader use.

items.q: Which report-widget categories can I use?
items.a: The Reports > Templates library organizes report widgets into categories so you can quickly find metrics related to a specific area of the firm.
more: Available categories include Revenue, Clients, Workflow, Tasks, Time, Billing, and Agreements. Each category can include different types of widgets, such as headline metrics, trend charts, aging reports, client or assignee breakdowns, operational lists, and budget-versus-actual views.

For example, a management dashboard could combine Total Revenue from Revenue, New Clients from Clients, Stage Aging from Workflow, Overdue Tasks from Tasks, Utilization from Time, A/R Aging from Billing, and Agreement Funnel from Agreements. Use Search when you know the widget you need, and use the category filters when you want to explore related measures and identify additional widgets for your dashboard.

items.q: How does the dashboard help identify work needing attention?
items.a: The Overview dashboard helps firm users identify work that may require attention by bringing key deadlines, exceptions, workload indicators, and operational risks into one place.
more: Depending on the widgets available to your firm, the dashboard can highlight items such as approaching or missed deadlines, stalled engagements or workflow bottlenecks, review work waiting for action, unsigned engagement letters, overdue tasks, team workload or capacity pressure, outstanding receivables, and important filing dates.

The information displayed can also support different roles across the firm. Partners and firm leaders may focus on revenue, receivables, client concentration, workflow bottlenecks, and overall firm performance. Managers and reviewers may prioritize engagement progress, review queues, deadlines, overdue work, and team capacity. Team members may focus on assigned tasks, upcoming deadlines, engagement activity, and work requiring follow-up.

Select a dashboard tile, metric, or record to open the related area in AssurePro and review the underlying work. For example, an overdue invoice can lead to Billing, a workflow bottleneck can lead to Workflow, an awaiting-signature item can lead to Engagement Letters, and a workload alert can lead to Team & Roles. The dashboard is designed to act as an operational starting point, helping each user quickly identify the work most relevant to their role and move directly to the area where action is required.

items.q: What is included in AssurePro Settings?
items.a: Settings is the central administration area for configuring how AssurePro works for your firm.
more: Settings covers firm profile and branding, client portal configuration, teams, roles, and permissions, workflows and work standards, documents and reusable templates, billing and financial controls, notifications and reminders, connected-service integrations, security and access settings, and the reusable defaults used during onboarding and service delivery.

It is organized into five groups: Firm (identity, branding, organizational setup), Work (workflows, documents, templates, and work-related configuration), Finances (billing and financial settings), Communication (notifications, email, and automated reminders), and Access (users, permissions, security, and connected services). For example, use Firm Profile to manage branding, Workflow to configure delivery stages, Reminders to manage automated follow-up, and Integrations to manage connected services.

items.q: How do I find a particular setting?
items.a: Use Search settings when you know what you want to configure but are unsure where the setting is located.
more: The Settings area is organized into Firm, Work, Money, Communication, and Access. Search settings looks for matching Settings pages and lets you open the relevant page directly. For example, search "reminders" to find automated follow-up settings, search "credentials" to find the firm's secure credential-management area, search "documents" to find document-related configuration, and search "notifications" to find notification and email settings.
steps: Open Settings from the Admin area of the main navigation.
Enter a keyword in Search settings, or browse the available setting groups.
Select the matching Settings page from the results.
For example, you can open Documents under Work or Notifications & Email under Communication.

items.q: What should an administrator configure first?
items.a: A firm administrator should begin with the settings that define the firm, its users, and how client work will be managed in AssurePro.
more: A recommended setup order is:
Firm Profile — add the firm's name, contact information, branding, and client-facing identity.
Team & Roles — add partners, managers, and other firm users, then assign the appropriate roles and permissions.
Engagement Types — define the services your firm provides, such as tax, bookkeeping, advisory, or other engagement types.
Workflow — configure the stages used to manage work from initiation through preparation, review, completion, and delivery.
Documents — define document-related settings and reusable document configurations used across client engagements.
Tags — create labels that help the firm organize and filter clients, engagements, and work.
Onboarding Defaults — configure reusable defaults that help standardize how new clients and engagements are set up.
After the core practice-management setup is complete, configure the relevant billing, communications, integrations, and access settings used by your firm.

Before rolling the configuration out across the practice, test it with an internal or demo client. Run the client through a typical process such as onboarding, engagement setup, document collection, workflow, review, communication, time tracking, and billing. This helps confirm that the setup reflects how your firm actually operates before it is applied more broadly.

items.q: What can we maintain in Firm Profile?
items.a: Firm Profile is where firm administrators maintain the firm information and branding used across AssurePro and supported client-facing experiences.
more: You can maintain information such as firm name, firm logo, phone number and email address, website, mailing address, EIN, primary and accent brand colors, and client-facing branding.
The firm logo can be uploaded in PNG, JPG, WEBP, or SVG format, up to 1 MB, with a minimum recommended size of 256 × 256 pixels.
steps: Open Settings > Firm Profile.
Upload, replace, preview, or remove the firm logo.
Review and update the firm name, phone number, email address, website, mailing address, and EIN.
Select the primary and accent colors used in supported client-facing areas such as the client portal, emails, and documents.
Use the client-facing preview to confirm that the firm's branding and information appear correctly.
Confirm that the page shows your changes as saved before leaving.
Keeping Firm Profile up to date helps ensure that clients see consistent and accurate firm information across their interactions with your practice.

items.q: How is the client portal address configured?
items.a: Firm administrators can configure the web address clients use to access the firm's client portal from Settings > Client Portal.
more: AssurePro provides a standard portal URL for the firm. Administrators can configure the firm-specific URL slug and, if preferred, add a custom domain such as portal.yourfirm.com to provide a more branded client experience.
The portal URL slug can contain lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, up to 63 characters. AssurePro checks the URL for availability when it is saved.
steps: Open Settings > Client Portal.
Enter the required Portal URL slug and select Save URL.
Use Copy beside the current default URL when you need to share the active client portal address.
To use a branded portal address, enter your custom domain, such as portal.yourfirm.com, and select Add domain.
Complete any domain verification or activation steps shown in AssurePro.
Continue using the active standard portal URL until AssurePro confirms that the custom domain is active.
Once configured, the portal address can be provided to clients so they can access the firm's client-facing portal for supported activities and interactions.

items.q: How are teams, members, invitations, and roles managed?
items.a: Firm administrators manage user access and responsibilities from Team & Roles.
more: This area includes three main tabs:
Teams — group firm users who work together or share similar responsibilities. Teams can also be used for work assignment, client access, workload visibility, and shared operating settings.
Members — shows active firm users, including their product access, assigned team or role, account status, and permission count.
Invitations — tracks invitations sent to new firm users, including the team selected, date sent, and whether the invitation is pending, accepted, or cancelled.

Roles define reusable permission sets that can be assigned to firm users based on their responsibilities. For example, a partner, manager, reviewer, or preparer role may carry a different level of access.

When reviewing a user's access, use the product selector to confirm which AssureOne products the user can access. A firm user may have access to AssurePro but different permissions or no access to AssureTax, AssureAudit, or AssureBooks.
Keeping teams and roles aligned with job responsibilities helps the firm apply access consistently and avoid managing permissions one user at a time.

items.q: What can be configured for a team?
items.a: Firm administrators can configure teams in AssurePro to group users with similar responsibilities and define how they access client work.
more: A team can include the team name and description, a standard hourly rate when the firm uses a common rate for that team, client-access scope, team members, and the permissions required for the team's responsibilities. If Access all clients is enabled, members of the team can access clients across the firm, subject to their permissions; if it is not enabled, client access follows the firm's client-assignment rules.

Teams should generally be created around job functions or service responsibilities, rather than individual exceptions. For example, a tax-preparation team may need access to assigned tax clients, client documents, tasks, and workflows, while not requiring firm-wide billing, administrative, or security permissions.
steps: Open Team & Roles > Teams.
Select New team, or select Manage for an existing custom team.
Enter the team name and description.
Set the standard hourly rate, if your firm uses one for the team.
Choose whether the team should have Access all clients.
Add the appropriate firm users to the team.
Select the permissions required for the team's responsibilities.
Review the client-access scope and permissions, then save the team.
Review team membership and permissions periodically, especially when a person's responsibilities, service lines, or client assignments change.

items.q: How granular are team permissions?
items.a: AssurePro allows firm administrators to control team permissions by both work area and action, so access can be aligned with each team's responsibilities.
more: Permissions are organized across areas such as Client Management, Content & Documents, Work & Operations, Communication, Finance & Compliance, Reporting & Analytics, and Administration. For supported work areas, administrators can grant specific actions such as View, Create, Edit, Delete, and Assign.

This allows the firm to give users only the access they need for their role. For example, a firm user may be allowed to view billing information without being able to create, modify, or cancel invoices, while a firm administrator may have access to firm-wide settings, user management, and security controls. Review permissions based on job responsibilities before adding or inviting users, and avoid granting broader access than is required for their day-to-day work.

items.q: How do administrators review members and invitations?
items.a: Team & Roles lets administrators review both active firm users and people who have been invited but have not yet completed activation.
more: The Members tab can be searched by name or email and filtered by role; each row shows product access, assigned role or team, account status, and permission count. Use the product selector when reviewing access, since a person's permissions can differ across AssurePro, AssureTax, AssureAudit, and AssureBooks.
The Invitations tab shows the recipient, assigned team, date sent, and status for everyone invited to the firm; a pending invitation can be resent or cancelled.
steps: Open Team & Roles > Members.
Search by name or email, or filter by role.
Review the person's product access, role or team, account status, and permission count.
If the person is not active, open Invitations and check whether an invitation is still pending.
Resend the invitation if needed, or cancel it if it's no longer required.

items.q: How do I invite a team member?
items.a: Firm administrators can invite partners, managers, accountants, reviewers, and other firm users from Team & Roles.
more: Before sending the invitation, select the appropriate team and role so the new user receives the access needed for their responsibilities. The invitation remains visible in the Invitations tab until the user completes account activation.

After receiving the invitation, the user opens the most recent invitation email, verifies the invited work email address, and creates a password. Once activation is complete, the user appears under Members with the assigned role, team, and product access.
steps: Open Settings > Team & Roles, or select Team & Roles from the main navigation.
Select Invite member.
Enter the user's name and work email address.
Select the appropriate team and role based on the user's responsibilities.
Review the assigned access and send the invitation.
Use the Invitations tab to monitor invitations that are still pending.
If an invitation is still pending, review or resend the existing invitation rather than creating a duplicate. This helps avoid multiple activation emails for the same user.

items.q: What are Engagement Types?
items.a: Engagement Types are reusable definitions for the services your firm delivers to clients. They help standardize how different types of client work are created and managed in AssurePro.
more: Engagement Types can be organized under service areas such as Bookkeeping, Audit & Assurance, Accounting, Advisory, and Tax. Each Engagement Type can include a name, description, code, and service-specific configuration, and it can also define the Custom fields used to capture information relevant to that type of engagement.
For example, your firm may create Engagement Types such as Individual Tax Return, Business Tax Return, Monthly Bookkeeping, Financial Statement Audit, and Advisory Engagement.

When a firm user creates new client work, they select the appropriate Engagement Type instead of starting from a blank engagement. This helps the firm apply a consistent service structure and capture the information required for that type of work. Using standardized Engagement Types also makes it easier to organize, assign, manage, and report on similar engagements consistently across clients.

items.q: How do I configure an engagement type's Custom fields?
items.a: Firm administrators can configure Custom fields for each Engagement Type to capture information specific to that type of client work.
more: Available field types include Dropdown, People, Date, Files, Number, Money, Formula, and Text. For example, a tax engagement may use Custom fields for the filing year or entity type, while a bookkeeping engagement may use fields for the accounting period, assigned reviewer, or other service-specific information.

Custom fields can be reordered or deleted. Depending on the field type, administrators can also configure options such as Required or Active/Inactive. Formula fields are calculated automatically and are read-only for firm users.
steps: Open Settings > Engagement Types.
Select the Engagement Type you want to update.
Select Add field and choose the required field type.
Enter the field label and complete the available configuration.
For Dropdown fields, add the available choices.
Set the Required and Active options where supported.
Use Move up or Move down to arrange the Custom fields in the preferred order.
Review any required, inactive, or read-only indicators.
Open an engagement using that Engagement Type and confirm that the Custom fields appear and behave as expected.
Keep Custom fields focused on information your firm needs to prepare, review, manage, or report on the engagement, so data collection stays standardized without adding unnecessary data entry.

items.q: What are Onboarding Defaults?
items.a: Onboarding Defaults allow firm administrators to define the standard setup applied when a new client is created in AssurePro.
more: These defaults reduce repetitive setup and help ensure new client records are created consistently across the firm. Administrators can preconfigure items such as the default assignee for the client's first engagement, a default engagement letter template, and a default client folder structure.
For example, your firm can automatically assign a standard onboarding owner, apply the usual engagement letter template, and create the same folder structure for each new client.
steps: Open Settings > Onboarding Defaults.
Select the Default assignee for the first engagement, or leave it unset if your firm wants AssurePro to resolve the assignee automatically.
Select a Default engagement letter template, or choose None (auto-resolve) when appropriate.
Select the Default folder structure for new clients.
Choose None only if new clients should be created without a predefined folder structure.
Confirm that the page shows All changes saved.
Onboarding Defaults should reflect your firm's standard onboarding process; client- or engagement-specific requirements can still be adjusted on the individual client or engagement.

items.q: How are tags created and maintained?
items.a: Tags help your firm categorize and organize clients and engagements in AssurePro. They can be used to make records easier to identify, filter, and group based on characteristics that matter to your practice.
more: For example, your firm might use tags for service type, client segment, industry, priority, location, or other internal classifications.
Firm administrators can create, rename, and delete tags from Settings > Tags.
steps: Open Settings > Tags.
Enter the new tag name under Add a tag.
Select Add Tag.
To rename an existing tag, select Edit and update the tag name.
To remove a tag, select Delete after confirming that it is no longer required on client or engagement records.
Use a consistent naming convention when creating tags and avoid creating multiple tags that represent the same category. This helps keep filtering and reporting consistent across the firm.

items.q: How do I configure personal notification preferences?
items.a: Firm users can manage their own notification preferences from Settings > Notifications & Email.
more: AssurePro provides separate email and in-app notification options for events such as new document uploads, client messages, invoice payments, upcoming deadlines, overdue invoices, and emails received in a connected client inbox. You can choose one or both notification channels for each event type.

For example, you may enable both email and in-app notifications for high-priority items such as upcoming deadlines or overdue invoices, while using only in-app notifications for routine activity that you typically review while working in AssurePro.
steps: Open Settings > Notifications & Email.
Review each notification type.
Turn Email and In-app notifications on or off based on how you want to receive that alert.
Select Save Preferences.
Choose notification settings that match how you work so important client, billing, and deadline-related activity is visible without creating unnecessary alerts.

items.q: How do report alerts work?
items.a: Report alerts help firm users monitor important KPIs without having to review reports manually throughout the day.
more: An alert can either notify selected firm users when a metric reaches a defined threshold or send a scheduled summary of key firm metrics.
Report alerts can be delivered by email and through the in-app notification bell.
Two alert types are available:
KPI threshold — sends an alert when a selected metric meets the condition and threshold you define.
Scheduled digest — sends selected firm metrics on a recurring schedule.

For example, a firm may create a threshold alert when overdue receivables exceed a certain value or use a scheduled digest to provide partners and managers with a regular summary of operational or financial KPIs.
steps: Open Settings > Notifications & Email.
Go to Report alerts and select New alert.
Enter an alert name.
Choose KPI threshold or Scheduled digest.
For a threshold alert, select the metric, condition, threshold value, and reporting window.
Select the firm users who should receive the alert.
Create the alert.
Review existing alerts in the Report alerts list.
Use report alerts for metrics that require timely attention, and keep the subscriber list focused on the partners, managers, or other firm users responsible for acting on the information.

items.q: What is in the Template Library?
items.a: The Template Library provides reusable starting points that help CPA firms standardize recurring work and client communication in AssurePro.
more: The library can include templates for engagement letters, workflows, client folder structures, and messages. Firm users can preview a template before adding it to the firm's library, and after it is added, the firm can edit its working copy to reflect its own services, policies, workflow standards, and client communication style.
For example, a firm may start with a standard tax engagement letter, bookkeeping workflow, client folder structure, or client reminder message and then adapt it before using it in day-to-day work.

Before adding a template, review its description, tags, and included content to confirm that it matches the firm's intended use. Once added, open the template in the relevant editor and customize it before using it with clients.

items.q: How do I find the right Template Library item?
items.a: Use the search, filters, and asset-type tabs in the Template Library to quickly narrow the available templates to the type of work your firm is setting up.
more: You can search by name, type, or tag, filter by practice area, review only templates already added to the firm, and sort the available results.
steps: Open Template Library from Admin.
Select All, Engagement Letter Templates, Workflows, Folders, or Messages to narrow the library by template type.
Search by name, type, or tag.
Select a practice area to focus on templates relevant to that service line.
Turn on Added only to review templates that have already been added to your firm's library.
Use Sort to change the order of the results.
Select Preview to review the template's details and included content before adding it.

Use Search when you already know the type of template you need. Use the practice-area filters and template tabs when you want to explore available options for a particular service, such as tax, bookkeeping, audit, or advisory work.

items.q: How do I add and customize a Template Library item?
items.a: Firm users can add a curated item from the Template Library and then customize the firm's working copy before using it in live client work.
more: The original library item remains unchanged. Your firm edits the copy that is added to the appropriate working area in AssurePro.
steps: Open the template and select Preview.
Review the template's practice-area and entity tags, along with the available summary of its packages, services, workflow stages, tasks, folders, or communication channel.
Select Add to Library.
Use the available Open in… option to open the added copy in the appropriate area: Engagement Letters, Workflow, Folder Templates, Messages.
Review and update the firm's copy to reflect your services, internal processes, billing approach, document structure, or client communication standards.
Save and test the customized template before using it with clients.
Treat curated templates as starting points rather than final firm-approved content. Review each added copy carefully so it aligns with your firm's policies and operating standards.

items.q: What does each Template Library type provide?
items.a: The Template Library includes different template types that help your firm standardize recurring client work, documents, and communication.
more: Engagement Letter Templates provide reusable agreement content and can include service packages, services, and billing structures used when setting up client engagements. Workflows provide reusable stages and tasks that define how work moves from setup through preparation, review, completion, and delivery. Folder Templates provide standardized client folder structures so documents are organized consistently across similar engagements or services. Message Templates provide reusable email or SMS content for common client communications, such as reminders, document requests, follow-ups, and status updates.

These template types can be used together to standardize an end-to-end service. For example, an Engagement Letter Template can define the agreed services and billing structure, a linked Workflow can define the operational stages and tasks, a Folder Template can establish the document structure, and Message Templates can standardize recurring client communications throughout the engagement.

items.q: How is a new client added directly?
items.a: Create a client directly in AssurePro when the relationship is already confirmed and the client does not need to move through the prospect pipeline.
more: The client record becomes the central starting point for managing the firm's relationship with that client, including contacts, portal access, documents, engagements, assignments, billing, and other client work.
steps: Open Clients and select New Client, or choose Client from the global + New menu.
Enter the required Client Name and Entity Type.
Add any applicable details such as status, industry, sub-industry, assigned firm users, folder template, country, and address.
Optionally add the primary contact's name, phone number, and email address.
Choose whether Send portal invite should remain selected for the client.
Review the client information and select Create Client.
After the client is created, review the client record to confirm the appropriate contacts, firm assignments, portal access, folders, and onboarding defaults have been applied correctly.

items.q: What are all the ways to add a client?
items.a: AssurePro provides several ways to add a client, depending on how the relationship was established and how the firm is onboarding the client.
more: You can add a client by:
Creating the client directly — use this when the relationship is already confirmed and the client does not need to move through the prospect pipeline.
Converting a prospect to Won — use this when the client originated as a lead or prospect and you want to preserve the prospect history.
Importing clients in bulk — use a CSV or Excel file when onboarding or migrating multiple client records.
Creating a client while starting an engagement — use this when the required client does not yet exist and you need to create the record as part of the engagement setup.
Using the global + New menu — provides a shortcut to the standard direct-client creation form.
Choose the method that best preserves the client's history and avoids duplicate records.

For example, use direct creation for an established client, prospect conversion for a qualified lead, bulk import for a migration or prepared client list, and contextual creation when setting up an engagement for a client who is not yet in AssurePro.
Regardless of how the client is added, review the resulting client record for contacts, firm assignments, portal access, folder structure, and onboarding defaults before beginning live client work.

items.q: How do I convert a prospect into a client?
items.a: Convert a prospect to a client when the opportunity has completed your firm's prospect process and the relationship has been confirmed.
more: Moving the prospect to Won preserves the prospect history and transitions the record into client onboarding, so the information already captured does not need to be recreated.
steps: Open Prospects and locate the lead in Board or List view.
Open the prospect record and review the information that should carry forward, such as: Company and contact details, Service interest, Assigned owners, Deal value, Expected close date, Tags, Notes.
Open the Stage control and change the prospect to Won.
Open the resulting client record.

Complete any client-specific information that was not captured during the prospect stage, including: Firm assignments, Contacts, Portal access, Documents and folder structure, Engagement setup, Other onboarding details.
Using the Won stage helps your firm maintain continuity from prospecting through onboarding while preserving the history of the relationship.

items.q: How do I import multiple clients?
items.a: Use the client import feature when your firm needs to add or migrate multiple client records into AssurePro at the same time.
more: AssurePro supports CSV and XLSX files. A downloadable CSV template is also available to help your firm prepare client data in the expected structure before uploading it.
steps: Open Clients.
Select More ways to add clients, then choose Import from CSV.
Download the provided CSV template if you need guidance on the expected file structure, or prepare a supported .csv or .xlsx file.
Upload the file by dragging it into the import window or selecting it using the file browser.
Review any validation messages or data issues identified during the import.
Complete the import once the file is ready.
Review the imported client records to confirm that the information has been created correctly.
After the import, review important client information such as contacts, entity details, firm assignments, portal access, folder structure, and onboarding defaults before beginning live client work.

For large migrations, it is a good practice to test the import with a small sample first so your firm can confirm the file structure and resulting client records before importing the full client list.

items.q: Can I create a client while starting an engagement?
items.a: Yes. If the client record does not yet exist, firm users can create it directly while setting up a new engagement.
more: The New Engagement client selector includes a Create new client option, so you can continue the engagement setup without leaving the workflow.
This is useful when the engagement is ready to be created but the client has not yet been added to AssurePro.
steps: Open Workflow and select New Engagement.
Open the Client selector.
Select Create new client.
Enter the required client information and create the client record.
Return to the engagement setup.
Select the newly created client and the appropriate Engagement Type.
Complete the remaining engagement details and save the engagement.

After the engagement is created, open the client's Info tab and complete any additional information that was not captured during the quick client-creation step, such as contacts, entity details, portal access, firm assignments, or relationship information.

items.q: What can firm users see in a client workspace?
items.a: The client workspace gives firm users a consolidated view of the client relationship and the work associated with that client.
more: Depending on your firm's configuration and access, the workspace can include areas such as Overview, Info, Documents, Communications, Engagements, Billing, Engagement Letter, Credentials, Emails, and AI SOP. The Overview provides a concise operating summary of the client, including items that may require attention, open work, upcoming deadlines, document activity, balances, communications, and recent activity.

Use the specialized tabs when you need to work with the full underlying record. For example, review overdue invoices or balances in Billing, review an unsigned engagement package in Engagement Letter, check missing or uploaded source files in Documents, review active work, assignments, and delivery progress in Engagements, and review client communication history in Communications or Emails.
The client workspace helps partners, managers, reviewers, and firm users move between different parts of the client relationship without having to search for or reopen the client record each time.

items.q: What information is kept on the client Info tab?
items.a: The Info tab stores the core profile and relationship information for a client.
more: Depending on the client's entity type and your firm's configuration, the tab can include profile completeness, contact information, entity details, Contacts, Tags, Related Entities, Account Roles, and Notes. The fields shown can vary based on the client type — for example, an individual client may include information such as SSN, date of birth, filing status, address, and applicable period, while a business client may display different entity-specific information.

The Info tab keeps the primary client record separate from related people and entities: use Contacts for people associated with the client, Related Entities for connected businesses or other entities, Account Roles to identify each person's relationship or responsibility, Tags to categorize the client, and Notes for additional internal context.

Keeping these areas separate helps your firm maintain accurate client records. For example, when a business has multiple owners, employees, or related companies, update the appropriate contact or relationship record instead of replacing information on the primary client profile.

items.q: Can a client have multiple contacts and relationship details?
items.a: Yes. A client record can include multiple Contacts, Related Entities, and Account Roles, allowing your firm to maintain the different people and relationships associated with the client without combining them into the primary client record.
more: For example, a business client may have separate contacts for an owner or partner, bookkeeper or controller, payroll contact, accounts payable contact, authorized signer, and other client representatives. Related Entities can be used to record connected businesses or entities, while Account Roles help identify the role or relationship each person has with the client.

Keeping these relationships separate allows firm users to work with the correct person or entity when managing client communications, portal access, document requests, engagement activity, and other client-facing work. For example, an engagement letter may need to go to an authorized signer, while a bookkeeping document request may need to go to the client's bookkeeper — maintaining separate contacts and roles helps your firm direct each interaction to the appropriate person.

items.q: How does AssurePro help complete a client profile?
items.a: The Info tab includes a profile-completeness checklist that helps firm users identify missing client information during onboarding and ongoing account maintenance.
more: The checklist can highlight missing details such as contact information, mailing address, entity information, filing or reporting period, and other required client-profile fields. Firm users can complete the missing information directly from the client record.

Treat profile completeness as an onboarding quality check, not just a completion score. Maintaining a complete and accurate client profile helps support downstream work such as engagement setup, document requests, client communications, engagement letters, billing, and reporting. Before starting live client work, review the checklist and complete the information your firm needs for that client and service.

items.q: Can a portal invitation be sent again?
items.a: Yes. Firm users can resend a client portal invitation when a client has not completed activation or needs a new invitation link.
more: Before resending the invitation, confirm that the correct contact is being invited and that the email address on the client record is accurate.
steps: Open the client record and select Info.
Locate the contact who should have portal access.
Confirm that the contact's email address is correct.
Select Resend invite.
Ask the client to open the most recent invitation email and complete the activation steps, including email verification and password setup where prompted.
Confirm successful portal access using the available portal-access status or client activity history.
If multiple invitation emails have been sent, the client should use the newest one because an older invitation link may no longer be valid.

items.q: What can a client do through the client portal?
items.a: The client portal gives clients a secure, client-facing space to complete the activities your firm makes available to them.
more: Depending on the services and features enabled, clients can review and sign engagement letters, respond to document requests, upload requested files and supporting documents, exchange messages with the firm, review invoices, and pay invoices when online payment is enabled.

Portal access typically begins with an invitation sent during client onboarding or from the client's Info tab. A common client workflow is to accept the portal invitation, set up account access, review requests from the firm, upload required documents, sign the engagement package, and pay an invoice when online payment is enabled.

Clients see only the information and actions made available through the client-facing portal. They do not have access to the firm's internal AssurePro workspace, internal notes, assignments, or other firm-only information.

items.q: Does a client set a password for the client portal, or use a passwordless link?
items.a: Clients create an account password when activating their AssurePro client portal access. The invitation email is used to begin account activation; it is not a permanent passwordless sign-in link.
more: The client typically opens the invitation sent to their email address, accepts the invitation, completes email verification when prompted, creates a password, and then uses the verified email address and password for future portal or mobile-app access. Client access activity, such as invitation acceptance or portal sign-in, may also appear in Recent Activity, giving firm users operational visibility into the activation process.

If a client reports that the invitation link no longer works, first confirm that the correct email address is stored on the client record, then resend the portal invitation from the client's Info tab. Ask the client to use the most recent invitation email, complete any verification steps shown, and create or confirm their password before signing in again.

items.q: Is there a mobile app for clients?
items.a: Yes. AssurePro provides a client mobile app for iOS and Android so clients can complete supported activities from a mobile device.
more: Depending on what the firm makes available, clients can use the app to review requests from the firm, upload documents, exchange messages, review and sign documents, and review invoices or complete supported billing actions. A client must accept the firm's portal invitation and activate their account before using the app.
steps: Ask the client to open the invitation sent by the firm and complete account activation, including email verification and password setup.
Install the AssurePro client app on an iOS or Android device and sign in with the same client account.
Confirm that the relevant request, message, signing package, or invoice is available to the client before asking them to act.

items.q: Can we migrate data from our previous practice-management software?
items.a: Yes. The AssureOne implementation team can work with your firm to plan and execute a migration from an existing practice-management system into AssurePro.
more: The exact migration scope is agreed during implementation and depends on factors such as the source practice-management system, available export formats, client and contact records to be migrated, historical information required by the firm, documents or other supporting data included in scope, field mapping between the source system and AssurePro, data quality and cleanup requirements, and cutover timing and rollout approach. The implementation team works with your firm to determine what information can be migrated and how it should map into AssurePro.

Before the migrated data is used for live client work, your firm should review and validate key records, including client information, contacts, assignments, and other agreed migration data. Migration requirements can vary significantly between firms, so the final scope, validation process, and cutover plan should be agreed as part of the implementation process.

items.q: Does AssurePro include CRM capabilities?
items.a: Yes. AssurePro includes CRM capabilities that allow your firm to manage both prospects and active client relationships within the same practice-management environment.
more: For prospects, firm users can capture and manage prospect and contact details, assigned owner, lead source, service interest, expected close date, deal value, tags, qualification information, and notes and prospect activity. Prospects can then be managed through the firm's sales pipeline until the opportunity is won or otherwise closed. For example, your firm can add a referral as a prospect, assign a relationship owner, record the services being discussed, track the expected value and close date, and move the opportunity through stages such as Discovery and Proposal.

When the prospect is moved to Won, the relationship can continue into client onboarding without recreating the client from the beginning. The resulting client workspace can then support contacts and relationship information, client portal access, documents, engagements and workflows, engagement letters, communications, and billing. This helps your firm maintain continuity from the initial prospect relationship through onboarding and ongoing client service.

items.q: How are prospects managed before they become clients?
items.a: AssurePro allows your firm to manage prospects through a configurable sales pipeline before they become clients.
more: Prospects can be viewed in either Board or List view: Board view provides a visual view of prospects by pipeline stage and allows firm users to move opportunities as they progress, while List view makes it easier to search, filter, and compare prospect information across multiple opportunities.

Your firm is not limited to a single predefined sales process — firm administrators can create pipelines and configure their stages to match how the practice qualifies, scopes, proposes, and closes new work, and stages can be added, renamed, reordered, or restructured to match how the firm actually sells. For example, a general pipeline might include New Lead, Discovery, Qualified, Proposal, Decision, and Won / Lost. Your firm can also maintain different pipelines for different service lines: an advisory pipeline may include Assessment and Scoping, while a tax pipeline may use stages that reflect the firm's tax-client acquisition process.

Within each prospect record, firm users can manage prospect and contact details, assigned owner, service interest, tasks and follow-up activities, notes, emails and calls, deal value, expected close date, tags and qualification information, and engagement letter activity. The selected pipeline also provides visibility into measures such as lead count, pipeline value, won opportunities, won value, win rate, and average deal size, helping partners and other responsible firm users monitor business-development activity.
steps: Open Prospects and select the pipeline used for the relevant service line or sales process.
If needed, create or configure the pipeline and arrange its stages in the order your firm follows.
Use Board view to review and move prospects through stages, or List view to search, filter, and compare prospect records.
Open a prospect to update its owner, service interest, tasks, notes, communications, deal information, expected close date, and other qualification details.
Review pipeline metrics to understand the volume, value, and progress of prospective work.
When the opportunity is accepted, move the prospect to Won.

AssurePro then converts the prospect into a client record and carries forward the relevant prospect information into the client relationship, so firm users do not need to recreate the client from the beginning.

Open the new client record and complete any client-specific information that was not captured during the prospect stage, such as portal access, firm assignments, folder structure, contacts, or engagement setup.

Moving a prospect to Won should be treated as the transition from business development to client onboarding. The prospect history is retained for continuity, while ongoing client work is managed from the client record.

items.q: How do I create a prospect?
items.a: Create a prospect in AssurePro when your firm wants to track a potential client before the relationship is confirmed.
more: A prospect can be added directly to the appropriate sales pipeline and stage, along with the information your firm needs to qualify, follow up, and manage the opportunity.
steps: Open Prospects and select New prospect.
Enter the required prospect name and email address.

Add any additional information that applies, such as: Company, Phone number, Pipeline and stage, Lead source, Assigned owner, Deal value, Expected close date, Tags, Lead type, Referrer, Industry, Company size, Job role or designation, Service interest, Linked contact.
Review the information and select Add prospect.
Confirm that the prospect appears in the intended pipeline and stage.
Review the assigned owner and expected close date, then add a task, note, or other next action where appropriate.

As the opportunity progresses, update the prospect record and move it through the relevant pipeline stages. When the opportunity is accepted, move the prospect to Won so AssurePro can convert it into a client record while retaining the relevant prospect history.

items.q: What information can be captured for a prospect?
items.a: A prospect record can store the information your firm needs to qualify, manage, and follow up on a potential client before the relationship is converted into an active client.
more: Standard prospect information can include contact and company details, pipeline and stage, lead source, assigned owner, expected close date, deal value, service interest, tags, lead type and referrer, industry and company size, job role or designation, and notes and qualification information.

If the standard prospect fields do not capture information required by your firm's business-development or onboarding process, administrators can add Custom fields in Settings — for example, for the current accounting or practice-management system, number of entities, annual revenue range, fiscal year-end, tax jurisdictions, audit requirement, current service provider, preferred onboarding date, or other firm-specific qualification criteria.

Use clear field names and consistent field types so partners, managers, and business-development users capture information in the same way across prospects. Well-designed Custom fields also help preserve useful qualification information when the prospect is converted to a client, reducing the need to collect the same information again during onboarding.

items.q: What work can be managed from a prospect record?
items.a: A prospect record gives firm users one place to manage the information and activities associated with a potential client before the relationship becomes active.
more: Depending on your firm's configuration, the prospect record can include the following areas. Overview: key prospect, ownership, qualification, and pipeline information. Tasks: follow-ups and next actions assigned to firm users. Email: prospect-related email communication. Calls: calls and outreach activity. Engagement Letters: engagement-letter activity prepared during the proposal or closing process. Notes: internal notes from discovery calls, meetings, and other interactions. Pipeline and Stage: the prospect's current position in the firm's sales process.

Firm users can also maintain the assigned owner, service interest, deal value, expected close date, tags, qualification details, and other firm-defined prospect information. Use the prospect record as the working history of the opportunity so tasks, communications, notes, and qualification details remain connected as the prospect moves through the pipeline.

items.q: What is a typical prospect workflow in AssurePro?
items.a: A prospect typically moves through a series of pipeline stages as your firm qualifies the opportunity and determines whether it should become a client.
more: For example, a pipeline can run Prospect, Discovery, Proposal, then Won or Lost. A typical process: Prospect captures the lead, assigns an owner, records service interest, and creates the first follow-up task; Discovery documents calls and meetings, captures qualification details, and updates the expected deal value or close date; Proposal defines the proposed services, manages follow-up actions, and prepares or tracks the engagement letter.

Won is used when the prospect has accepted the opportunity and is ready for client onboarding — AssurePro converts the prospect into a client record and carries forward the relevant prospect information. Lost is used when the opportunity will not proceed; the prospect stays available for historical reference but is not converted into a client. Firm users should keep updating the prospect's stage, next actions, communications, and notes as the opportunity progresses.

items.q: How are documents organized across the firm?
items.a: AssurePro organizes documents at both the firm level and the client level so users can quickly find missing, requested, uploaded, and completed documents.
more: At the firm level, the Documents screen groups document activity by client and can highlight clients that are still waiting on required documents. Within an individual client workspace, documents are organized into folders and can be reviewed by source or purpose, including client uploads, document requests, engagement letters, tax returns, source documents, signed forms, correspondence, messaging-related files, and other miscellaneous documents.

Use the firm-level Documents view to identify clients with outstanding document needs, then open the client workspace to review the actual files, folder structure, and request history. To keep document management consistent across the practice, use Folder Templates to standardize folder structures, use Document Types to classify documents consistently, and use available source filters to distinguish client uploads, requested documents, internal files, and imported files. This structure helps partners, managers, reviewers, and firm users locate the right documents without searching across separate client records or systems.

items.q: Can firms standardize folder structures and document labels?
items.a: Yes. Firm administrators can use the Documents settings to standardize how client files are organized and classified across the practice.
more: The available configuration includes Folder Templates, Document Types, and Work Types. Administrators can use these settings to define reusable folder structures and document classifications, including folder names and hierarchy, document codes, document labels, categories, descriptions, custom fields, and active or inactive status.

For example, a tax folder template might include Intake, Source Documents, Workpapers, Review, Filed Return, and Correspondence. Document Types can then be used to classify files such as W-2, 1099, K-1, identification documents, signed forms, or other tax records.

Applying these standards during onboarding helps ensure that firm users work with a consistent document structure across similar clients and engagements. It also gives clients a more predictable experience when they are asked to upload or review documents.

items.q: How do I create or update a folder template?
items.a: Firm administrators can create reusable Folder Templates to standardize how documents are organized for clients and recurring service types.
more: A folder template should reflect a repeatable service or engagement structure rather than the needs of one exceptional client.
steps: Open Settings > Documents.
Stay on the Folder Templates tab.
Select New template to create a new structure, or open an existing template to update it.
Enter the template name and any other available details.
Use Add Folder to create the required folders and build the hierarchy.
Arrange the folders in the order and structure your firm wants users to follow.
Save the template.
Apply the template to a demo or internal client from the client's Documents tab to confirm that the folder names and hierarchy appear as expected.
If the template should be applied automatically to future clients, select it under Settings > Onboarding Defaults.

For example, your firm may maintain separate folder templates for Individual Tax, Business Tax, Monthly Bookkeeping, Audit, or Advisory work so teams follow a consistent document structure across similar clients.

items.q: What can be configured for Document Types?
items.a: Document Types help your firm classify files consistently and define the information that should be captured for each type of document.
more: Firm administrators can maintain document categories and create firm-specific Document Types with a name, description, category, code or label, custom fields, and active or inactive status. System-provided Document Types are identified separately from the definitions created by your firm.

For example, your firm may maintain Document Types for items such as W-2, 1099, K-1, bank statement, identification document, signed engagement letter, or tax return. Each type can then carry the classification and additional information your firm needs when organizing or reviewing documents. Use clear and consistent Document Type names so partners, managers, reviewers, and firm users classify similar documents in the same way across clients and engagements.

items.q: What is available under Work Types in Documents settings?
items.a: Work Types define the categories of client work that can be used when your firm creates document-intake templates.
more: They help organize document collection around the type of service being performed, such as Bookkeeping, Audit & Assurance, Accounting, Advisory, and Tax. AssurePro includes system-provided Work Types, and firm administrators can also create additional custom Work Types when the standard options do not match the firm's service structure.

A custom Work Type can include a code, label, description, and active or inactive status. For example, your firm may create separate Work Types for Individual Tax, Business Tax, Monthly Bookkeeping, Payroll, Financial Statement Audit, or Advisory work. Set a Work Type to Inactive when it should no longer be available for new document-intake setup, while preserving its use on existing documents.

items.q: How is a folder template applied to a client?
items.a: Firm users can apply a Folder Template from the client's Documents tab to quickly create the standard folder structure used for that client or service.
more: Applying a template adds the saved folders to the client workspace. It does not prevent firm users from adding additional folders when a client has requirements that fall outside the standard structure.
steps: Open the client record and select Documents.
Select Apply Template.
Choose the Folder Template that matches the client's service, engagement, year, or reporting period.
Review the folders that will be added.
Apply the template.
Use New Folder if the client needs an additional folder that is not part of the standard template.

For example, a tax client may receive a standard structure such as Intake, Source Documents, Workpapers, Review, Filed Return, and Correspondence, and additional client-specific folders can still be added to it.
If the same Folder Template should be used for most new clients, select it during client creation or configure it under Settings > Onboarding Defaults.

items.q: How do I request documents from a client?
items.a: Use a document request when your firm needs the client to provide specific files or information through the client portal.
more: The request tells the client what is needed, where to provide it, and when it is due. Files uploaded in response remain connected to the request and the client workspace, allowing firm users to track outstanding items without relying on separate email follow-up.
steps: Open the client record and select Documents.
Select Request.
Describe each document or item the client needs to provide.
Select the destination folder where the returned files should be stored.
Set the due date and complete the recipient and other request details shown in the form.
Review the request and confirm that it is being sent to the correct client contact.
Send the request.
Use the Requests view to monitor outstanding and completed requests.
The client receives the request through the client-facing experience and can upload the requested files against it. Once received, the documents remain available in the client's Documents workspace.
For example, your firm might request W-2s, 1099s, bank statements, payroll reports, identification documents, or other source documents required for an engagement.

items.q: What happens if a client doesn't respond to a document request?
items.a: If a document request remains outstanding, AssurePro can follow the firm's configured Document requests reminder schedule to remind the client automatically.
more: Firm administrators can control whether these reminders are enabled and configure items such as the initial delay, reminder frequency, and number of reminders sent.
steps: Open Settings > Reminders.
Confirm that Document requests reminders are enabled.
Review or update the: Initial reminder delay, Repeat interval, Total number of reminders.
Monitor the request from the client's Documents > Requests view.
If the request remains outstanding after the automated reminder sequence, follow up with the client directly.
Use Communications to keep the follow-up connected to the client relationship where appropriate.
Automated reminders help reduce routine follow-up work, while firm users can still step in when a deadline is approaching, a client needs clarification, or the requested documents remain outstanding.

items.q: What is the difference between Request, Import, and Upload?
items.a: Use Request, Import, or Upload based on who currently has the document and where the file is stored.
more: Request: use when the client still needs to provide the document — AssurePro sends a document request through the client experience and tracks the response. Import: use when the document already exists in a supported connected storage service, such as OneDrive or Dropbox. Upload: use when a firm user already has the file on their computer and wants to add it directly to the client workspace.

For example, use Request when the client still needs to provide a W-2, use Import when the W-2 already exists in the firm's connected OneDrive or Dropbox account, and use Upload when a firm user has the W-2 saved locally. Before completing any of these actions, confirm that you are working in the correct client record and select the appropriate destination folder so the document is stored in the right location.

items.q: How do I upload a document to a client workspace?
items.a: Use Upload when a firm user already has the document saved locally and needs to add it to a client's Documents workspace.
more: Before uploading, confirm that you are working in the correct client record and destination folder so the file is stored in the right location.
steps: Open Documents and select the client.
Choose the destination folder in the folder tree. If the required folder does not exist, create one using New Folder.
Select Upload.
Choose the file from your computer.
Confirm the destination and complete the upload.
Open the uploaded file from the client workspace to verify that the correct file was added.
If multiple versions of a document exist, check the filename and file contents after upload to make sure the final or intended version was stored.

If the uploaded file is meant to satisfy an outstanding document request, also review the client's Requests view. A general file upload may not automatically complete or match the outstanding request unless it is associated with that request.

items.q: How do I import documents from Dropbox or OneDrive?
items.a: Firm users can import documents from a connected Dropbox or OneDrive account directly into a client's Documents workspace.
more: The storage provider must first be connected to AssurePro. If no supported storage integration is configured, AssurePro directs the user to Settings > Integrations before cloud import can be used.
steps: Open Settings > Integrations.
Connect the firm's supported Dropbox or OneDrive account if it has not already been configured.
Return to Documents and select the appropriate client.
Choose the destination folder where the imported files should be stored.
Select Import.
Choose the connected storage provider and select the required files.
Complete the import.
Review the client's document list to confirm that the correct files were imported into the intended folder.
Use Import when the required documents already exist in your firm's connected cloud storage. This avoids downloading the files locally and uploading them again manually.

items.q: How do I find a file or review outstanding requests?
items.a: Use the Files view to find documents already stored in a client workspace, and use the Requests view to review document requests that are still outstanding or have been completed.
more: In the Files view, firm users can search and filter documents by filename, folder, source, and file type. Source filters can help distinguish documents that were Requested from files that were added internally.
steps: Open Documents and select the client.
Use the folder tree or All Documents to define where you want to search.
Search by filename.
Use the source filter, such as All, Requested, or Internal, to narrow the results.
Apply the file-type filter or switch between list and grid view when helpful.
Switch to Requests to review items that are still awaiting a client response or to review completed requests.
If a file you expect to find does not appear, clear or reset the active filters before uploading another copy. This helps reduce duplicate documents in the client workspace.

items.q: Can client documents be organized by tax year or reporting period?
items.a: Yes. Your firm can organize client documents by tax year, fiscal year, month, quarter, or other reporting period.
more: Firm administrators can include period-based folders in a Folder Template, while firm users can also create additional folders directly in the client's Documents workspace. For example, a recurring client may use a structure such as Tax > 2025 > Source Documents / Workpapers / Filed Return, or Bookkeeping > 2026 > January / February / March.

AssurePro does not require every firm to follow one fixed folder structure — your firm can choose the convention that best matches its services and operating process. Before rollout, decide whether the period should be reflected in the folder structure, filename, engagement record, or a combination of these, and use the same convention consistently across similar clients.

Using a consistent year- or period-based structure makes it easier for preparers, reviewers, and managers to locate the correct documents and reduces the risk of working from files belonging to the wrong period.

items.q: Can documents be brought in from cloud storage?
items.a: Yes. AssurePro supports document import from connected Dropbox and OneDrive storage.
more: Firm users can bring documents into a client workspace without first downloading them to a local computer and uploading them again. There are two common ways to use connected cloud storage. Import: use this for a one-time selection of files from a connected Dropbox or OneDrive account. Synced folder: use this when new files placed in a connected cloud folder should continue to flow into the client's Documents workspace. For example, use Import when you need to bring in a set of historical source documents once, and use a synced folder when your firm or client regularly places new files into a designated cloud-storage location.

Before importing or configuring a sync, confirm the correct client and destination folder — a connected Dropbox or OneDrive account may contain files for multiple clients, so verifying the destination helps prevent documents from being stored against the wrong client record. Cloud storage must first be connected under Settings > Integrations before Import or synced-folder functionality is available.

items.q: What views are available for engagement work?
items.a: The Workflow area provides three main views for managing engagement work:
more: Board — shows engagements by workflow stage and is useful for understanding where work is in the process and moving engagements between stages.
List — displays engagement information in rows and is useful for searching, filtering, sorting, and comparing engagement details.
Tasks — focuses on actionable tasks across engagements so firm users can review work that needs to be completed.
Firm users can switch between these views without changing the underlying engagement.

For example, a manager may use Board to identify work accumulating in Review, switch to List to compare due dates and assignments, and use Tasks to see the specific actions that are still outstanding.

The Workflow area also allows users to select a workflow, search for engagements, create a new engagement, customize the information displayed, and open the related workflow configuration where permitted.

items.q: What does the Workflow board show?
items.a: The Workflow Board gives firm users a visual view of engagements grouped by their current workflow stage.
more: Depending on the information configured for the workflow, engagement cards and stage summaries can show the engagement name and client, current workflow stage, priority, assigned roles or firm users, due date, start date, time spent in the current stage, engagement value, task-completion progress, and active or overdue work. For example, a manager may see a high-priority 1040 engagement in the Review stage along with its assigned reviewer, due date, number of days in Review, engagement value, and completed-task progress.

Stage-level totals can also help managers identify broader operational issues — one overdue engagement may require individual follow-up, while multiple overdue engagements accumulating in the same stage may indicate a workflow bottleneck or capacity issue. The Overview dashboard can complement the Workflow Board by surfacing open, due-soon, past-due, stalled, and review-related work that may require attention.

items.q: How are engagement workflows configured?
items.a: A workflow defines the repeatable process the firm follows to deliver an engagement from start to completion, including its stages, their order, the requirements for advancing, and the tasks created as work reaches each stage.
more: For example, a workflow may run Intake, Document Collection, Preparation, Review, Client Approval, Complete. A strict stage can require its gates to be satisfied before an engagement advances; a flexible stage lets firm users move work forward with fewer mandatory controls. Reusable task templates make the workflow operational: when an engagement enters a stage, AssurePro can create its predefined tasks, assign them to the right role, and calculate due dates relative to the date the engagement entered that stage.
steps: Open Settings > Workflow, then open an existing workflow or select New Workflow.
Name the workflow and add the stages that represent the firm's delivery process.
Drag the stages into the order work should progress.
Configure each stage as strict or flexible, and add any stage gates or progression requirements.

Add reusable task templates to the appropriate stages; for each one, enter a clear task name, assign the responsible role, set its relative due date, and mark it Required when completion should be mandatory.
Arrange the tasks in the order firm users should follow, then save the workflow.
Test it with a demo engagement and confirm the stages, tasks, assignments, due dates, and progression controls behave as intended.
After rollout, use each stage's active and overdue counts to identify recurring delays and refine the workflow.

items.q: How do I create a workflow?
items.a: Firm administrators can create a workflow from Settings > Workflow to define the standard process used for a recurring type of engagement.
steps: Open Settings > Workflow.
Select New Workflow.
Enter a clear workflow name that identifies the service or process it supports.
Add the required workflow stages.
Arrange the stages in the order the engagement should follow.
Configure any stage gates or progression controls.
Add task templates to the appropriate stages.
For each task, select the responsible role, set the relative due date, and mark it as required where appropriate.
Save the workflow.
Create a demo engagement that uses the workflow.
Confirm that the stage order, generated tasks, assignments, due dates, and progression rules appear as expected before using it for live client work.
For example, your firm may create separate workflows for Individual Tax, Business Tax, Monthly Bookkeeping, Audit, or Advisory engagements when the delivery process differs across service lines.

items.q: What can be configured on workflow task templates?
items.a: Workflow task templates define the repeatable tasks that AssurePro creates when an engagement reaches a particular workflow stage.
more: Firm administrators can configure each task template with a task name, responsible role, relative due-date offset, required status, and task order within the stage.
