The relative due date is calculated from the date the engagement enters the stage, helping the firm create a consistent timeline for recurring work.

For example, an Intake stage may include a required task such as Confirm signed engagement letter before the engagement can move to Document Collection. Administrators can add, edit, delete, and reorder task templates within each workflow stage. Use clear task names that describe the expected deliverable, assign the role responsible for completing the work, and mark a task as Required when the engagement should not advance without it.

items.q: What is Firm SOP and how is it managed?
items.a: Firm SOP is the central location for maintaining firm-wide standard operating procedures in AssurePro.
more: It helps your firm document repeatable processes so partners, managers, reviewers, and firm users can follow a consistent approach when performing recurring work. The Firm SOP area separates procedures by status: All, Pending, Active, Draft, and Rejected. Use Draft while a procedure is being written or revised, Pending when it is ready for review, Active when it has been approved for firm use, and Rejected when it should not be used.
steps: Open Settings > Firm SOP.
Select New SOP.
Enter and document the procedure.
Save it as Draft while it is being prepared.
Move it to Pending when it is ready for review.
Mark it Active once the procedure has been approved for use across the firm.
Use Rejected when the procedure should not be adopted.

Use Firm SOP for procedures that apply broadly across the practice. Keep client-specific instructions in that client's AI SOP area so exceptions or unique client requirements remain separate from firm-wide standards.

items.q: How is a new engagement created?
items.a: Firm users can create a new engagement either from Workflow or from the client's Engagements tab.
more: When the engagement is created, the selected Engagement Type determines the workflow structure and other configured defaults that apply to that type of work, such as stages, tasks, roles, and dates.
steps: Select New Engagement.
Search for and select the client.
If the client does not yet exist, select Create new client and complete the required client information.
Select the appropriate Engagement Type.

Enter the engagement details shown for that type, such as the engagement name, start and due dates, priority, assigned roles or firm users, recurrence for a repeating engagement, and any other fields specific to that Engagement Type.
Select Create Engagement.
Open the new engagement and review the configured: Workflow stages, Tasks, Role assignments, Due dates, Other engagement details.
Creating the engagement from the client's Engagements tab starts the process with that client already selected, which can be useful when firm users are already working in the client workspace.
Before beginning live work, confirm that the Engagement Type, assignments, dates, and generated workflow match the service your firm is delivering.

items.q: How should firm users use Board, List, and Tasks views?
items.a: The Board, List, and Tasks views provide different ways to review the same underlying engagement work. Switching views does not change an engagement's status or workflow.
more: Use each view based on the question you are trying to answer:
Board — use when you want to understand where engagements are in the workflow. It is useful for reviewing stage volume, overdue work, assignments, due dates, time in stage, and task progress.
List — use when you need a compact, record-level view for searching, filtering, sorting, or comparing multiple engagements.
Tasks — use when you want to focus on the individual work items that need to be completed across engagements.
steps: Open Workflow and select the workflow you want to review.
Choose Board to review engagement progress by stage and identify work that may be stalled or overdue.
Choose List to search and compare engagement-level information.
Choose Tasks to review actionable work items and their status.
Open the relevant engagement or task from any view when you need to review or update the underlying work.

For example, a manager may use Board to identify several engagements accumulating in Review, switch to List to compare their due dates and assigned reviewers, and then use Tasks to see the specific review work that remains outstanding.

items.q: Can an engagement repeat?
items.a: Yes. AssurePro supports recurring engagements for services that repeat on a regular schedule.
more: Depending on the engagement setup, recurrence can be used for work such as monthly bookkeeping, quarterly advisory, payroll-related work, periodic accounting services, and other repeatable client engagements. Recurring engagements can display recurrence indicators such as monthly or semesterly, occurrence counts, and a Finished repeating state when the recurrence has ended.

When setting up recurrence, confirm the recurrence pattern, the starting period, the client and Engagement Type, assigned roles or firm users, engagement dates, workflow stages, and tasks and due dates. Each generated occurrence should follow the intended structure so firm users do not need to rebuild the same engagement manually for every period.

Use recurrence when the underlying service and workflow are expected to repeat consistently. If the client's scope or delivery process changes significantly between periods, review the engagement setup before relying on the recurring configuration.

items.q: How are tasks tracked?
items.a: Tasks in AssurePro represent the individual actions that need to be completed as part of client and engagement work.
more: A task can include a task name, priority, due date, assignee or responsible role, completion status, related client or engagement, and workflow context. Tasks can appear in several places across AssurePro, including Workflow, the client Overview, Tasks views, and dashboard task and review widgets. Overdue tasks are highlighted separately so managers and firm users can identify work that has passed its due date.

A well-defined task should describe one clear action, have an accountable owner or role, and include a meaningful due date. For example, Review uploaded W-2s can be assigned to the reviewer on a client's tax engagement, marked as high priority, tracked within the engagement, and surfaced as overdue if it is not completed by the due date. Keeping tasks specific and properly assigned helps preparers, reviewers, and managers understand what needs to happen next and who is responsible for completing it.

items.q: Can standard operating procedures be managed in AssurePro?
items.a: Yes. AssurePro supports documented procedures at different levels so your firm can maintain consistent working practices while still accounting for service- or client-specific requirements.
more: Use the appropriate SOP location based on where the procedure applies. Firm SOP: use for policies and procedures that apply broadly across the practice. Service-level SOP: use for procedures that define how a particular service or type of work should be delivered. Client AI SOP: use for instructions, exceptions, or working procedures that apply only to a specific client.

Firm SOPs can use statuses such as Draft, Pending, Active, and Rejected. Draft: the procedure is still being written or updated. Pending: the procedure is ready for review or approval. Active: the procedure is approved and should be followed by firm users. Rejected: the procedure should not be used.

For example, your firm may maintain a firm-wide SOP for client data handling, a service-specific SOP for preparing individual tax returns, and a client AI SOP for a client that requires a unique review sequence or document-handling process. Separating procedures by scope helps firm users follow the correct instructions without mixing firm-wide standards with client-specific exceptions.

items.q: How does the time tracker work?
items.a: The time tracker allows firm users to record time as work is being performed and keep that time connected to the correct client, engagement, task, and billing treatment.
more: Use Start when you want AssurePro to track elapsed time while you work. If the time is already known, you can enter the duration manually instead. For client work, the time entry can include the client, engagement, task, work date, description, billable or non-billable status, and duration. Capturing these details when the work is recorded helps reduce cleanup later during billing, time review, and reporting.
steps: Open the time tracker from the application header.
Choose Client work or Internal work.
For client work, select the client and the related engagement.
Select an existing task or create the task associated with the work.
Select Start to begin live time tracking, or enter the hours and minutes manually.
Confirm the work date and add a clear description of the work performed.
Mark the entry as Billable or Non-billable, as appropriate.
Save the entry.
Review the entry in Time Sheet, where information such as duration, rate, amount, billable status, and invoice status is available.
For accurate billing and reporting, record time against the correct client, engagement, and task whenever possible.

items.q: Can time be entered manually instead of using the timer?
items.a: Yes. Firm users can enter time manually when live tracking was not used or when the duration of the work is already known.
more: Manual time entry is useful for situations such as work completed away from the live timer, time recorded from another reliable work record, corrections to a previous entry, or work entered after it was completed.
steps: Open the time tracker.
Choose Client work or Internal work.
For client work, select the correct client, engagement, and task.
Enter the actual hours and minutes worked.
Select the date on which the work was performed.
Add a description that clearly explains the work completed.
Choose Billable or Non-billable.
Review the applicable rate, where relevant.
Save the entry.
Review the entry in Time Sheet and confirm its duration, amount, assignee, billable status, and invoice status before it is included in billing.
Manual entries should reflect the actual work performed and the correct work date so time-based billing, utilization reporting, and engagement records remain accurate.

items.q: How does AssurePro support workload, capacity, and budget oversight?
items.a: AssurePro brings together team workload, workflow progress, recorded time, and reporting so partners and managers can see where work is at risk and decide when reassignment, follow-up, or a budget review is needed.
more: The clearest picture comes from reading the views together: Team load shows how work is distributed and who is overloaded; Workflow shows where engagements are sitting, for how long, and where bottlenecks are forming; Time Sheet shows the actual effort recorded, including billable, non-billable, invoiced, and uninvoiced time; and Reports or a custom dashboard show utilization, capacity, and budget-versus-actual results where the firm tracks engagement budgets.

For example, if Team load shows a reviewer as overloaded with several overdue tasks, a manager can open Workflow to see engagements waiting in Review, check Time Sheet to see whether more hours than expected have already been used, then reassign lower-complexity reviews, adjust due dates, and follow up with preparers on engagements needing rework.
steps: Use Team load to compare assigned task volume, overdue work, and members whose workload is marked as overloaded.
Use Workflow to review how long engagements have sat in each stage, task progress, due dates, and bottlenecks.
Use Time Sheet to compare actual hours recorded by client, engagement, task, or assignee.
Open the Time & Utilization or Workflow & Capacity dashboard for broader trends, adding a budget-versus-actual widget when the firm tracks engagement budgets.
Take the appropriate action — reallocate tasks, adjust assignments or due dates, or investigate an engagement overrun — and repeat the review on a regular cadence.

items.q: What can we do in Time Sheet?
items.a: Time Sheet is the detailed register for reviewing recorded time across the firm and moving eligible billable time into invoicing.
more: Firm users can review time by date, client, engagement, task, or assignee; see start time, end time, duration, description, rate, and amount; distinguish billable from non-billable time; identify invoiced and uninvoiced entries; search, filter, and group entries for comparison; correct entries before billing, subject to permissions; generate invoices from eligible billable time; and export time data for external analysis or reconciliation.

For example, a manager preparing monthly billing can filter to one client, group by engagement, show only billable and uninvoiced time, correct any incomplete entries, and select the approved time for Generate invoice. Always check invoice status before selecting time for billing — an entry already linked to an invoice should not be billed again.

items.q: How can a new signing package be started?
items.a: A new signing package can be started in one of the following ways:
more: Start from scratch — use this when the engagement terms, services, pricing, or agreement wording are unique.
Use a saved firm template — use this for repeatable services where your firm already has an approved structure.
Use a curated template — use this as a reviewed starting point that your firm can adapt before sending it to a client.

Choose the starting method based on how standardized the engagement is. For example, a recurring monthly bookkeeping engagement may be best created from a saved firm template, while a complex advisory engagement with unique commercial terms may be better started from scratch.
Regardless of the starting method, review the client, recipients, services, pricing, agreement wording, billing terms, and approval requirements before sending the package.

items.q: What are the main steps in the engagement-letter builder?
items.a: The engagement-letter builder guides firm users through four connected sections so the client, commercial terms, agreement content, and sending requirements can be reviewed before the package is issued.
more: Setup answers who the package is for; Services & Pricing defines what is being offered and how the client is charged; Agreement & Terms holds the agreement wording and supporting content; Review & Send confirms dates, reminders, billing, and approvals before sending. The progress indicator lets firm users return to an earlier section without losing the package in progress.
steps: Setup: confirm the client, signing-package name, primary recipient, and any additional recipients or signers.
Services & Pricing: add the services, packages, add-ons, pricing, discounts, billing method, and any client-selectable options; review the selections against what the firm intends to deliver.

Agreement & Terms: configure the agreement wording and supporting terms, including additional terms, PDFs or attachments, firm notes, approval requirements, and payment-capture steps; review any edited language carefully.
Review & Send: confirm the recipients, sign-by and validity dates, reminder cadence, selected services, pricing and total, billing arrangement, and approval requirements.
Use Preview to review the package from the client's perspective, then resolve every item in the missing-requirements list; Send remains unavailable until the required information is complete.

items.q: How do I create and send an engagement letter?
items.a: Create an engagement letter in AssurePro by starting a new signing package from Engagement Letters.
more: You can build the package from scratch or start from a saved firm template or curated template, then tailor the client, recipients, services, pricing, agreement terms, and delivery settings before sending.
steps: Open Engagement Letters and select New signing package.
Choose whether to: Start from scratch, Use a saved firm template, Use a curated template.
In Setup, select the client, enter the package name, and confirm the primary and any additional recipients.
In Services & Pricing, add the services, packages, pricing, billing method, and any options the client can choose.
In Agreement & Terms, review the engagement-letter wording, approval requirements, supporting content, and any additional terms.
Select Preview to review the package as the client will see it.
In Review & Send, confirm: Recipients and signers, Sign-by date, Validity or expiration date, Reminder schedule, Services and pricing, Billing arrangement, Agreement terms, Approval requirements.
Review the missing requirements list and complete every required item.
Once all required information is complete, select Send package.
Send package remains unavailable until the required client, package name, recipients, services, pricing, agreement terms, and dates have been completed.
Before sending, use Preview as a final quality check to confirm that the client is receiving the correct services, pricing, terms, and signing instructions.

items.q: Can engagement letters be created and sent in bulk?
items.a: Yes. AssurePro allows firms to select a bulk draft engagement letter and send it to multiple clients.
more: Before sending, review the draft to confirm that the engagement-letter content, services, pricing, agreement terms, recipients, and signing requirements are correct for the selected clients — any client-specific information should be verified before the bulk send is completed.

To send engagement letters in bulk, open Engagement Letters, navigate to Drafts and select the engagement letter you want to send, review the included clients and engagement-letter details, confirm the recipients, services, pricing, dates, billing terms, and signature requirements, and select Send to send the engagement letters to the selected clients.
Bulk sending helps firms distribute a standardized engagement letter efficiently while still allowing the firm to review the draft and selected clients before sending.

items.q: How can services be presented to a client in a signing package?
items.a: In Services & Pricing, firm users can control how each service is presented to the client and whether the client has a choice.
more: Three presentation options are available: Client picks one, used when the client must choose one option from a set of mutually exclusive packages or services; Client can add it, used for optional services that the client may add to the engagement; and No client choice, used when the service is included automatically and the client is not expected to select or remove it. For example, use Client picks one for packages such as Basic, Standard, or Premium, use Client can add it for optional services such as an advisory consultation or additional support, and use No client choice for a service that forms a required part of the engagement.

The selected services, pricing, and billing terms remain part of the same signing package, giving the client a consolidated view of what is included and what they are agreeing to. Before sending, use Preview to confirm that the available choices, pricing, and resulting package structure are easy for the client to understand.

items.q: Can a package include more than one recipient?
items.a: Yes. A signing package can include a primary recipient and additional recipients when more than one person needs to review or sign the engagement letter.
more: This is useful for business clients or other engagements where multiple authorized individuals must participate in the signing process.
steps: In Setup, select the client.
Confirm the primary recipient.
Select Add additional recipient for each additional person who needs to receive or sign the package.
Review each recipient's name and email address.
In Review & Send, confirm the recipient list and applicable signing requirements.
Preview the package and send it when all required information is complete.
After the package is sent, firm users can monitor signing progress. If some, but not all, required recipients have signed, the package can show a Partial status.

For example, a business engagement may require both an owner and a second authorized signer. If the owner signs but the second signer has not yet completed their part, firm users can identify the outstanding recipient and follow up with that person rather than resending the entire package unnecessarily.

items.q: Can the firm customize the introduction and agreement terms?
items.a: Yes. Firm users can customize both the client-facing introduction and the agreement terms included in a signing package.
more: The introduction can use a predefined message or custom wording to explain the engagement and provide context to the client before they review the formal agreement. In Agreement & Terms, the firm can configure items such as the agreement or terms template, custom agreement wording, explicit approval requirements, additional text or supporting pages, PDF attachments, additional terms, firm notes, payment-capture steps, and approval automation where configured. Use the introduction for clear, client-friendly context about the relationship or engagement, and use the Agreement & Terms section for the formal terms governing the services.

Before sending, use Preview to review the complete package from the client's perspective, and confirm that any additional wording, attachments, or terms are consistent with the selected services, pricing, billing arrangement, dates, and approval requirements. For standardized engagements, consider maintaining approved firm templates so recurring legal and client-facing language does not need to be recreated for every package.

items.q: What is checked before a package is sent?
items.a: Before a signing package can be sent, Review & Send provides a final summary of the package and highlights any required information that is still missing.
more: Firm users should confirm the client, package name, primary and additional recipients, sign-by date, validity or expiration date, reminder cadence, selected services and client choices, pricing and discounts, billing arrangement, agreement terms, approval requirements, and any other required package details. AssurePro displays unresolved requirements in the builder and keeps Send unavailable until the required information is complete.

Treat the missing-requirements list as a pre-send quality check. Before sending, confirm that the package accurately reflects what your firm intends to offer and that the recipients, services, pricing, dates, billing terms, agreement wording, and approval requirements are correct. Use Preview as a final client-facing review before selecting Send package.

items.q: Can AssurePro remind a client to sign an engagement letter?
items.a: Yes. Firm users can configure a reminder cadence for a signing package so clients are reminded when an engagement letter is still awaiting action.
more: The reminder settings are configured in Review & Send along with the package's signing dates.
Before sending, confirm:
Sign-by date — when the client is expected to complete signing.
Validity or expiration date — how long the package remains available.
Reminder cadence — when reminders should be sent while action is still outstanding.
For example, your firm can set a sign-by date that aligns with the planned onboarding or engagement start date and choose a reminder cadence that gives the client appropriate time to respond.
Make sure the package does not expire before the intended reminder sequence has completed.

After sending, monitor the package status rather than relying on reminders alone. A client may already have viewed or partially signed the package even though the overall signing process is not yet complete.
Use the current package status to determine whether the client needs a general reminder or whether follow-up should be directed to a specific outstanding signer.

items.q: Which signing statuses can firm users track?
items.a: AssurePro allows firm users to track the progress of signing packages from preparation through completion.
more: Common package statuses include Draft, Sent, Viewed, Partial, Signed, Declined, and Archived. Draft: the package is still being prepared and has not been sent. Sent: the package has been sent to the intended recipient or recipients. Viewed: at least one recipient has opened or viewed the package. Partial: part of the required signing process has been completed, but one or more required signatures are still outstanding. Signed: all required signing actions have been completed. Declined: a recipient has declined the package. Archived: the package has been removed from the active working list while remaining available for historical reference.

The package record can also show supporting events or information such as date sent, viewed activity, partially signed activity, completion date, backdated activity, and consent status when consent is included in the package.

Use these statuses to guide follow-up. For example, a Sent package that has not been viewed may need a general client reminder, while a Partial package indicates that at least one required signer still needs to complete their action. A Signed package requires no further signature follow-up, while a Declined package may require the firm to contact the client and determine the next step.

items.q: How does the engagement-letter signature process work?
items.a: After the signing package is sent, the recipient opens the client-facing package, reviews the services, pricing, agreement terms, and any supporting content, then completes any required selections or approvals and signs by drawing a signature or typing their name.
more: AssurePro updates the package status as activity occurs — Sent, Viewed, Partial, Signed, or Declined. When multiple signatures are required, Partial means at least one required signer has acted but another is still outstanding. Once signing is complete, firm users can open the package from the client record or Engagement Letters to review the final accepted package, which retains the agreed services, pricing, terms, recipients, consent information, and signing activity.
steps: Before sending, confirm the correct client, recipients, services, pricing, agreement terms, sign-by date, and approval requirements.
The recipient opens the delivered client-facing package, reviews it, and completes any required selections, approvals, or consent steps.
The recipient signs by drawing a signature or typing their name and submits the package.
Track the package status — Sent, Viewed, Partial, Signed, or Declined — to know when to follow up.
Once complete, open the package from the client record or Engagement Letters to review the final accepted package and its recorded activity.

items.q: What are the magic link and audit log for a sent engagement letter?
items.a: For a sent engagement letter, the magic link gives access to that specific client-facing signing package, and the audit log records the delivery and signing activity for it.
more: The magic link is tied to one sent package — confirm the correct package and intended recipient before sharing it, and never reuse it for another client or package. The audit log can show when the package was sent, opened or viewed, signed, partially completed, or declined, helping firm users distinguish an access or delivery issue from a package that has simply not been signed yet.
steps: Open Engagement Letter and select the package from Sent, then preview the sent letter rather than reopening the draft builder.
Use the magic-link option to open or copy the client-facing link when a recipient needs help accessing it.
Confirm the package and intended recipient before sharing the link.
Open the audit log to review the package's recorded delivery and signing activity.

items.q: Can a client sign an engagement letter from a mobile device?
items.a: Yes. Clients can open and complete an engagement-letter signing package from a phone or tablet.
more: The mobile app allows the client to review the same client-facing information included in the package, such as the introduction, selected services and pricing, agreement terms, supporting pages or PDFs, required service selections, approval or consent steps, and payment-capture steps where included.
steps: Open the engagement-package on mobile app.
Review the introduction, selected services, pricing, agreement terms, and any supporting content.
Complete any required service selections, approvals, consent, or payment-capture steps.
Complete the signature by drawing it on the mobile screen or typing the signer's name.
Submit the completed package.
After the client acts on the package, firm users can monitor its progress using statuses such as Viewed, Partial, or Signed.

If more than one signer is required, a Partial status indicates that at least one required signer still needs to complete their part. Once all required signing actions are complete, the firm can open the completed engagement letter from the client record or Engagement Letters.

items.q: How is the Billing area organized?
items.a: The Billing area is organized into three main tabs:
more: Invoices — used to review receivables, agreement-generated drafts, invoice activity, and the invoice register.
Recurring — used to manage billing schedules that create invoices on a defined cadence.
Referrals — used to track MyCPEOne referrals and related commissions.
The Invoices tab is the main workspace for one-time and generated receivables. It includes summary cards, search, filters, and the detailed invoice register.
The Recurring tab is used when your firm wants billing to continue automatically on a recurring schedule.
The Referrals tab is used for MyCPEOne referral activity and commission tracking.

A signed-agreements banner can also surface billing items created from accepted engagement letters. These may include draft invoices or recurring schedules that still need firm review before they are activated or sent.
Use the Billing area based on what you need to manage: Invoices for receivables, Recurring for scheduled billing, and Referrals for referral-related activity.

items.q: What does the Invoices overview show?
items.a: The Invoices overview gives firm users a quick view of the firm's current receivables and billing activity.
more: Summary cards can include Outstanding, Overdue, Awaiting payment, Collected in the last 30 days, and Drafts. Selecting a summary card filters the invoice register to that group, making it easier to focus on the invoices that need attention. For example, select Overdue to review invoices that require collection follow-up, select Awaiting payment to review sent invoices that have not yet been paid, select Drafts to find invoices that still require review or completion, and select Collected to review recent payment activity.

The invoice register can also be searched by invoice number or client and filtered by status, client, source, and date range. Use Columns to control which invoice fields are visible in the register. A common workflow is to start with a summary card, then use search and filters to narrow the results to the specific client, invoice source, status, or period you need to review.

items.q: Which invoice sources and statuses are tracked?
items.a: The invoice register tracks both where an invoice came from and where it is in its lifecycle.
more: Source shows how the invoice was created: Manual from the invoice builder, Agreement from billing terms on a signed engagement letter, or Time from eligible billable time in Time Sheet. Status shows the invoice's lifecycle: Draft, Sent, Viewed, Overdue, Paid, or Cancelled. Total, remaining balance, and due date are shown separately, so status doesn't need to be inferred from the invoice amount — for example, a Time-source invoice marked Overdue tells the firm it originated from recorded time and still has an unpaid balance past its due date.

items.q: How is a new invoice created?
items.a: Create an invoice by selecting the client, setting the invoice and due dates, and adding at least one priced line item.
more: AssurePro keeps the send action unavailable until the required client, due date, and line-item information is complete.
steps: Open Billing and select Create invoice, or choose Invoice from the global + New menu.
Select the client, then select the related engagement when the invoice should be tied to a specific engagement.
Review the invoice number, issue date, and due date.
Add a service-catalog item or create a custom line item, then enter the quantity and unit price.
Import eligible unbilled time if the invoice includes time-based work, and add a discount or tax if the invoice needs one.
Add any relevant service description, client-visible note, or internal firm note.
Review the live invoice preview.
Choose Save as draft to review or complete the invoice later, or Create & send to issue it to the client.
Before sending, confirm that the client, engagement, services, quantities, rates, discounts, taxes, due date, and client-facing notes are correct.

items.q: What can firm users review on an individual invoice?
items.a: An individual invoice record gives firm users a detailed view of the invoice, its financial position, and the activity that has occurred since it was created.
more: Depending on the invoice, firm users can review the invoice status, invoice source, client, related engagement, invoice number, issue date, due date, subtotal, discounts, tax, total amount, amount paid, remaining balance, description, line items, related signed agreement for agreement-generated invoices, payment history, and audit trail.

The available action menu depends on the invoice's current status and permissions, and actions can include Download PDF, Edit, Send invoice, and Cancel. Use Payment history to reconcile payments received against the invoice, and use the audit trail to review important invoice events after creation. For an invoice generated from a signed engagement letter, use the related agreement link to compare the invoice with the services, pricing, and billing terms accepted by the client.

Before editing or cancelling an invoice, review its status, amount paid, and remaining balance. If a payment has already been recorded, confirm the appropriate billing treatment before making changes so the invoice record remains consistent with the payment history. This gives managers and billing users one place to understand both the original invoice and what has happened to it since it was issued.

items.q: How can clients pay an AssurePro invoice?
items.a: Clients can pay AssurePro invoices using the payment methods the firm enables through its connected payment processor.
more: Before online payment is available, the firm connects its payment processor under Settings > Integrations and confirms payout settings under Billing & Payments. The payment methods a client sees depend on the connected provider and the options the firm has enabled. After the client pays, the processor confirms the transaction and AssurePro updates the invoice's payment history, remaining balance, and status.

items.q: Can the firm record a payment received outside AssurePro?
items.a: Yes. Firm users can record a payment received outside AssurePro so the invoice balance and payment history remain accurate.
more: This is useful when a client pays through a method that is not processed directly through AssurePro, such as a check or another supported off-platform payment method.
steps: Open the relevant invoice.
Select Add payment.
Choose the payment method.
Enter the actual payment date.
Enter any required payment or reference details.
Review the information and save the payment.
Confirm that the payment appears in Payment history.
Review the remaining balance and invoice status to confirm that they were updated correctly.
For example, if a client pays an invoice by check, record the payment against that specific invoice using the actual payment date and applicable reference information.

Note: Record off-platform payments against the correct invoice before taking further billing action. This helps prevent the firm from following up on a balance that has already been paid or accidentally collecting the same amount twice.

items.q: Can signed agreements create billing work?
items.a: Yes. Billing terms accepted through a signed engagement package can generate billing work in AssurePro.
more: Depending on the agreement terms, AssurePro can create invoice drafts for one-time charges and recurring billing schedules for charges that repeat on an agreed cadence. The generated items appear in Agreements awaiting billing, where an authorized firm user can review them before an invoice is sent or a recurring schedule is activated. For example, a one-time engagement fee can generate an invoice draft, while a monthly bookkeeping agreement can generate a recurring billing schedule.

Because the billing work is generated from the accepted engagement terms, firm users do not need to manually recreate the agreed services, pricing, and billing structure. Before sending or activating the generated billing item, review the client, services, pricing, billing cadence, dates, and other commercial terms against the signed agreement. This creates a controlled handoff from signed engagement terms to billing, while still giving the firm an opportunity to validate the billing setup before it becomes active.

items.q: How do I review billing created by a signed agreement?
items.a: When a signed engagement letter creates billing work, AssurePro places the generated item in a review queue before it is sent or activated.
more: This gives authorized firm users a chance to confirm that the billing setup matches the client's accepted agreement.
steps: Open Billing and select the signed-agreements banner.
Search by client name or agreement name to find the billing item.
Under Pending review, review details such as: Signed date, Number of generated invoice drafts or recurring schedules, Amount.
Select Review & send.
Compare the generated billing item with the signed agreement, including: Client, Services, Line items, Pricing, Billing dates, Billing cadence, Related agreement.
Edit the draft or schedule if a correction is needed.
Send the invoice or activate the recurring schedule when the billing details are correct.
Use Active to review agreements that are already generating billing activity.

If an item is marked Manual, no priced services, the signed agreement does not contain automatically billable priced services. In that case, billing must be handled manually rather than generated from the agreement.
Reviewing agreement-generated billing before activation helps the firm confirm that the billing record matches the commercial terms the client accepted.

items.q: How does recurring billing work?
items.a: Recurring billing allows your firm to create invoice schedules for services that are billed on a repeating cadence.
more: A recurring schedule can include information such as client, service, billing cadence, amount, send mode, status, and next invoice date. Two send modes are available: Auto-send, where AssurePro creates and sends each scheduled invoice automatically, and Manual send, where AssurePro creates the invoice on schedule but a firm user reviews and sends it before it is delivered to the client. For example, a monthly bookkeeping engagement may use a Monthly schedule with Auto-send, while a quarterly advisory engagement may use Manual send so a manager can review the invoice before delivery.

Firm users can also manage an active schedule using actions such as Pause, which temporarily stops scheduled billing activity; Resume, which restarts a paused schedule; and Bill now, which creates an invoice immediately from an active schedule. Before activating a recurring schedule, confirm the client, service, amount, cadence, next invoice date, and send mode. Use Auto-send for stable, repeatable billing arrangements that do not require review each cycle, and use Manual send when pricing, scope, or client circumstances may need to be checked before each invoice is issued.

items.q: How do I review or control a recurring schedule?
items.a: Firm users can open a recurring billing schedule to review its current setup, billing history, and upcoming invoice activity.
more: The schedule details can include the client, client email, status, billing cadence, service, amount, next invoice date, total billed, total received, pending amount, and invoice history.
steps: Open Billing > Recurring.
Find the schedule in tile or list view.
Select View details.
Review the client, status, cadence, amount, next invoice date, totals, and invoice history.
Select Pause when scheduled billing should temporarily stop.
Select Resume when a paused schedule should begin running again.
Use Bill now when an immediate invoice is required from an active schedule.
Review any displayed future price change before the next scheduled invoice is generated.
Note: Bill now is unavailable while a recurring schedule is paused. Resume the schedule first if an immediate invoice needs to be created.
Before changing a schedule, review its next billing date and invoice history so the change does not result in an unintended duplicate or missed invoice.

items.q: What is the Services catalog?
items.a: The Services catalog is the firm's reusable library of services used across billing and engagement packages.
more: Instead of recreating the same service description, pricing, and billing setup each time, firm users can select an existing catalog item when preparing client work. Each service can include information such as the service name, description, kind, category, pricing model, default price or amount, discount and tax defaults, related SOP, and active or inactive status. The Services list can be searched and filtered by name or description, kind, pricing model, and active status. For example, your firm might maintain reusable services for Individual Tax Return, Monthly Bookkeeping, Tax Planning, Payroll, Audit Support, or Advisory Consultation.

Treat each catalog item as a standardized service definition. Name and description explain what the firm provides. Kind defines how the service is positioned or used. Category helps organize related services. Pricing model and default amount establish the starting billing structure. SOP documents how the service should be delivered. Active status controls whether the service is available for new work.
Maintaining a consistent Services catalog helps reduce pricing and service-description differences across engagement letters, invoices, and recurring client work.

items.q: Which service kinds and pricing models are available?
items.a: When creating a service, AssurePro separates its Kind from its Pricing model.
more: Kind describes the commercial role of the item: Service, Bundle, Add-on, Hourly, or Retainer. Pricing determines how the charge is calculated: Fixed, Hourly, or Retainer. For example, an Individual Tax Return can be a Service with Fixed pricing, an Advisory Consultation can use Hourly pricing, an ongoing advisory relationship can use Retainer pricing, Audit Protection can be an Add-on, and a tax-service package can be a Bundle containing several included services.

items.q: How do I create a service?
items.a: Create a service in Services to define a reusable offering that firm users can use in invoices and engagement packages.
more: A service can include its name, description, kind, category, pricing model, default price, discount, tax treatment, and related SOP.
steps: Open Services and select New service.
Enter the service name and, if needed, a description.
Choose the appropriate Kind: Bundle, Add-on, Hourly, Retainer, Service.
Select the appropriate Category.
Choose the Pricing model: Fixed, Hourly, Retainer.
Enter the default price or rate.
Add a default discount if your firm uses one.
Configure the default tax rate and whether the service is taxable.
Review the service details and select Create service.
Once created, the service becomes available as a reusable catalog item for supported engagement-letter and billing workflows.
Use clear, client-friendly service names and descriptions so the same definition can be reused consistently across the firm.

items.q: How do I find, deactivate, or archive a service?
items.a: Use search and filters in the Services catalog to find an existing service by name, description, kind, pricing model, or active status.
more: Firm administrators can then make a service inactive or archive it when it should no longer be used for new work.
Inactive — removes the service from normal selection for new work while keeping it available for reference and possible reactivation.
Archive — removes the service from normal catalog maintenance when it is no longer intended for active use.
steps: Open Services.
Search by service name or description, or filter by Kind or Pricing.
To deactivate a service, turn off its Active switch.
Enable Show inactive when you need to locate or reactivate an inactive service.
To archive a service, open the row action menu and select Archive.

Before deactivating or archiving a service, check whether it is referenced by: Engagement-letter templates, Draft or active agreements, Recurring billing schedules, Draft invoices, Other reusable firm configurations.
This helps prevent new client work from depending on a service that is no longer available for selection.

items.q: How is a standard operating procedure attached to a service?
items.a: A service can have a related Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) that documents how your firm performs and delivers that service.
more: The SOP helps preparers, reviewers, and managers follow a consistent process when the same service is delivered across multiple clients.
steps: Open Services.
Locate the required service.
Select the + control in the service's SOP column, or open the service's action menu and choose SOPs.
Add or update the procedure for that service.
Review the SOP to make sure the active instructions match the service currently being offered to clients.
For example, the SOP for Monthly Bookkeeping might document: Collect statements → Post transactions → Reconcile accounts → Complete review → Deliver reports → Follow up with client.
Use the service-level SOP for procedures that apply specifically to how that service is delivered. Keep broader firm policies in Firm SOP and client-specific exceptions in the client's AI SOP area.
Keeping the service description and SOP aligned helps ensure that what the firm sells and what the team delivers remain consistent.

items.q: How are time entries turned into invoices?
items.a: Billable time recorded in Time Sheet can become invoice line items in two ways: from Time Sheet, by selecting eligible uninvoiced entries and choosing Generate invoice, or from the invoice builder, by selecting Import unbilled time. Both let the firm use already-recorded time instead of re-entering hours.
more: From Time Sheet: filter to the correct client, engagement, task, assignee, or date range, show billable time, confirm the entries are not already invoiced, select them, and choose Generate invoice.

From the invoice builder: create or open an invoice for the client, select Import unbilled time, choose the eligible entries, and review the imported line items before sending. Always check invoice status before billing time — an entry already linked to an invoice should not be billed again.

items.q: What is the difference between Billing & Payments and Platform Subscription?
items.a: Billing & Payments and Platform Subscription serve two different financial purposes in AssurePro.
more: Billing & Payments covers money the firm collects from clients: invoice payments, connected payment processors, payment methods, payout accounts, and client receivables. Platform Subscription covers purchases the firm makes from AssureOne Technologies LLC, including platform charges, AI Credits, and the invoices and receipts AssureOne issues to the firm. A simple test: client pays the firm belongs under Billing & Payments; firm pays AssureOne belongs under Platform Subscription. Keep the two separate during reconciliation.

items.q: How do I review AssureOne platform purchases and receipts?
items.a: Use Platform Subscription to review invoices and receipts for purchases your firm makes from AssureOne Technologies LLC.
more: This area is separate from client billing and can show information such as the purchase or invoice, transaction date, status, amount, and payment-card summary.
steps: Open Settings > Platform Subscription.
Filter the purchase history by status or transaction date.
Locate the AssureOne purchase you want to review.
Select Preview to review the invoice or receipt on screen.
Confirm the amount, payment method, date, and purchasing firm details.
Select Download to save the invoice or receipt for your firm's records.
Store downloaded AssureOne invoices and receipts according to your firm's accounts-payable or expense-documentation process, rather than in a client's billing or document workspace.
This separation helps the firm distinguish its own software and platform expenses from amounts billed to or collected from clients.

items.q: What payment and accounting connections are available?
items.a: AssurePro supports integrations for both client payment collection and accounting synchronization.
more: Available connections include payment processor integration, used to collect client payments and manage the firm's payout connection, and QuickBooks Online, used to sync paid AssurePro invoices into the firm's accounting system. Firm administrators manage these connections from Settings > Integrations, and billing-related payout settings are also referenced under Billing & Payments.

A typical flow is to connect the firm's payment processor, confirm the payout account and payment configuration, send a test invoice or controlled transaction, verify that the payment is reflected correctly in AssurePro, and confirm that the corresponding paid-invoice information appears correctly in QuickBooks Online. Before relying on an integration for month-end reconciliation, test the connection with a controlled transaction and confirm that both AssurePro and the external system reflect the expected result.

items.q: Does AssurePro include referral tracking?
items.a: Yes. The Referrals tab under Billing allows your firm to track MyCPEOne referrals and the related commission activity.
more: The referral area can include information such as referred clients, referral status, active or paying referrals, related engagement, commission rate, monthly commission, lifetime earnings, total paid, accrued commission, and pending payout. Firm users can add referrals individually or use bulk import when multiple referrals need to be added.

For example, your firm can refer a client to MyCPEOne, associate the relevant engagement or service, and then monitor whether the referral becomes active or starts generating commission. The referral dashboard separates earned, accrued, paid, and pending amounts, helping the firm distinguish referral performance from commission cash already received.

items.q: How do I refer a client to MyCPEOne?
items.a: Firm users can create a MyCPEOne referral from Billing > Referrals.
more: The referral can be created for an existing AssurePro client or for a new referral contact that is not yet in the client list.
steps: Open Billing > Referrals.
Select Refer a client.
Choose: New client, From my clients.
Enter the required information, including: Client name, Entity type, Contact email, Service line.
Add any additional details that are useful, such as: Contact name, Phone number, Address, ZIP code, Requested services, Notes.
Review the referral details.
Submit the referral.
After submission, MyCPEOne can send the applicable client invitation, and the referral remains visible in AssurePro for status and commission tracking.
Review the referral record over time to monitor its status, related engagement, commission rate, accrued commission, and pending payout.

items.q: Which communication channels are available?
items.a: AssurePro brings the firm's client and internal communication channels together in Communications.
more: Available channels include Portal chat, Email, SMS, Calls, and Team chat. Portal chat: secure messages exchanged with clients through the AssurePro client experience. Email: client email communication sent through the firm's connected email service. SMS: text messages sent through the firm's connected Twilio number. Calls: client call activity that can be recorded as part of the communication history. Team chat: internal communication between firm users.

Firm users can work from the shared Communications area when they want to manage conversations across multiple clients, or open a client's Communications tab when they want to begin with that client already selected. Keeping these channels connected to the client record helps the firm maintain a more complete communication history across client service, document follow-up, billing, and engagement work.

items.q: How do I start a client conversation?
items.a: Firm users can start a conversation from the shared Communications area or directly from a client's Communications tab.
more: Starting from the client workspace is useful when you are already working with a specific client because the client is selected automatically.
steps: Open Communications, or open the client record and select Communications.
Select New Conversation.
Choose the client, if it is not already selected.
Choose the communication channel.
Complete the required information for that channel:
For Email, confirm the recipients, enter the subject, and write the message.
For Portal chat, confirm the client contact and enter the message.
For SMS, confirm the client contact and mobile number, then enter the message.
Review the recipients and message.
Send the conversation.
Use the shared inbox or client workspace to monitor replies and follow-up activity.
The conversation remains connected to the client relationship so other authorized firm users can review the communication history at any time.

items.q: What is the difference between portal chat and SMS?
items.a: Both portal chat and SMS let firm users communicate with clients, but the client receives and responds through a different channel.
more: Portal chat is delivered inside the AssurePro client experience — use it for an ongoing conversation with a client who has activated portal access. SMS sends a text to the client's mobile number through the firm's connected Twilio number — use it for short, time-sensitive messages such as deadline reminders, follow-ups, or prompts to check the portal. SMS requires the firm's Twilio connection, an enabled sending number, and any applicable messaging registration. Authorized firm users can review the communication history in AssurePro regardless of which channel was used.

items.q: How can the communications inbox be organized?
items.a: The Communications inbox can be filtered and organized so firm users can focus on conversations that need attention.
more: After selecting the relevant communication channel, you can narrow the inbox using All, Unread, Assigned to me, and Resolved. All: shows all conversations available to you. Unread: shows conversations with new activity that has not yet been reviewed. Assigned to me: shows conversations assigned to the signed-in firm user. Resolved: shows conversations that have been completed and no longer require active follow-up.

Labels can provide additional context about what should happen next. Needs Action: the firm needs to take the next step. Awaiting Reply: the firm has responded and is waiting for the client. FYI: the conversation is informational and does not currently require a response.

A practical daily workflow is to start with Assigned to me, prioritize conversations marked Needs Action, respond or complete the required work, and then update the thread appropriately. Use Awaiting Reply when the next action belongs to the client, and mark the conversation Resolved when no further follow-up is required. Consistent use of assignments, labels, and resolution status helps firm users at every level distinguish active client follow-up from conversations that are already complete.

items.q: Can client-facing emails be standardized?
items.a: Yes. Email Templates allows firm administrators to standardize automated emails that AssurePro sends on the firm's behalf.
more: Templates are organized by functional area, such as Billing, Tax & Intake, Documents, E-sign, Client Portal, and Internal Alerts. Each template is associated with a specific trigger, helping administrators understand when that message will be sent. Depending on the template, editable content can include the subject, heading, introduction, message body, call-to-action or button label, and footer.

For example, your firm can customize a billing email that tells the client an invoice is ready, a document-request email that explains what the client needs to upload, an e-sign email that asks the client to review and sign an engagement package, and a client-portal email used during account activation or other portal activity.

Standardizing these templates helps maintain consistent wording, tone, instructions, and branding across recurring client communications. When editing an automated template, keep the message specific to its trigger and avoid adding instructions that could conflict with the workflow or action the client will see after selecting the email's call-to-action.

items.q: How do I edit and test an automated email template?
items.a: Firm administrators can customize an automated email template from Settings > Email Templates and test the message before it is used with clients.
more: The template editor supports features such as supported placeholders for dynamic information, rich-text formatting, desktop preview, mobile preview, and test email delivery.
steps: Open Settings > Email Templates.
Search for the required email template or locate it within its functional group.
Review the template's trigger so you understand when the message is sent.
Edit the subject and any available message sections.
Use the { } control to insert supported placeholders where dynamic information is required.
Review both the desktop and mobile previews.
Select Send test to me to review the current message in an actual email.
Check the subject, formatting, wording, links or buttons, and placeholder placement.
Make any required corrections and save the template.
Confirm that the customized template appears under the Edited filter.

When testing, pay particular attention to placeholders. Make sure dynamic client, firm, date, invoice, document, or engagement information appears in a context that will still read naturally when the template is used.
Testing both desktop and mobile layouts helps ensure that clients receive a clear and usable message regardless of the device they use.

items.q: Can administrators audit automated email delivery?
items.a: Yes. Email Log gives firm administrators visibility into automated emails sent by AssurePro.
more: The log can show details such as sent time, delivery status, recipient, client, subject, message type, and delivery error when one is returned. Firm users can search the log by recipient or subject and filter by All, Sent, Failed, and Not sent. Use Sent to confirm successful delivery attempts, and use Failed or Not sent to identify messages that need investigation.

For example, if a client says they did not receive an automated document-request or engagement-letter email, search for the recipient and review the message status, timestamp, type, and any returned error. Verification-code and temporary-password emails are not included in Email Log.
For automated AssurePro messages, Email Log is the better source for delivery verification than relying on an individual firm user's sent-mail folder.

items.q: How do I investigate an email that was not delivered?
items.a: Use Email Log to investigate an automated AssurePro email that was not successfully delivered.
steps: Open Settings > Email Log.
Search by the client's email address or the email subject.
Filter the results to Failed or Not sent.
Review the: Recipient, Client, Sent time, Subject, Message type, Delivery error, when available.
Identify and correct the underlying issue, such as an incorrect email address, integration problem, or template-related issue.
Return to the workflow that originally generated the email, such as: Portal invitation, Invoice, Document request, Engagement-letter request.
Retry the action from that workflow.
Return to Email Log and confirm the new delivery attempt.
Do not assume that an email was delivered simply because the original workflow action was completed. Use Email Log to verify the status of the new attempt.
If the recipient address is incorrect, update the client or contact record before retrying so future automated communications use the correct address.

items.q: What reminders can be automated?
items.a: AssurePro can automate follow-up reminders for several common client actions, helping the firm reduce repetitive manual follow-up.
more: Reminder types can include document requests, unanswered messages, tax organizers, and signature requests. Document requests: reminds clients about requested files that are still outstanding. Unanswered messages: follows up when a client has not responded to a communication. Tax organizers: reminds clients to complete required intake or organizer information. Signature requests: follows up on engagement letters or other signing packages that remain unsigned.

Each reminder type has its own configuration, including an enable or disable control, an initial reminder delay, a repeat interval, and a total number of reminders, which allows the firm to use different follow-up schedules for different client actions. For example, a missing tax document may require a different reminder cadence from an unsigned engagement letter or an unanswered message.
Firm administrators should configure reminder schedules based on the urgency and expected response time of each workflow rather than using the same cadence for every type of client follow-up.

items.q: How do I change an automatic reminder schedule?
items.a: Firm administrators can configure each type of automated client reminder separately from Settings > Reminders.
more: Reminder schedules are available for document requests, unanswered messages, tax organizers, and signature requests. For each reminder type, your firm can control whether reminders are enabled and how frequently they are sent.
steps: Open Settings > Reminders.
Find the reminder type you want to update.
Turn the reminder on or off using the available switch.
Select Edit schedule.

Configure: Initial delay — number of days before the first reminder, Repeat interval — number of days between subsequent reminders, Maximum reminders — total number of automated reminders that can be sent.
Review the schedule summary displayed on the reminder card.
Set the cadence based on the type and urgency of the client action. For example, a time-sensitive tax organizer may require a different follow-up schedule from a routine document request.
Review reminder schedules periodically, particularly before high-volume filing or onboarding periods, to make sure the timing still matches your firm's client-service process.

items.q: Can AssurePro follow up when a client has not responded?
items.a: Yes. AssurePro can automatically follow up with clients when certain requests or actions remain outstanding.
more: Automated follow-up can be configured for document requests that are still awaiting files, unanswered messages waiting for a client response, tax organizers that have not been completed, and signature requests for unsigned engagement packages. Firm administrators configure the reminder schedule for each type independently, including the initial delay, repeat interval, and maximum number of reminders.

For example, if a client has not uploaded requested tax documents, AssurePro can send reminders according to the firm's Document requests schedule. If a client has not responded to an important conversation, the Unanswered messages schedule can provide a separate follow-up cadence.

Automated reminders reduce routine follow-up, but they do not replace active client management, and firm users should continue monitoring the underlying request, conversation, organizer, or signing package. If the automated reminder sequence ends and the item is still outstanding—or if the client reports a problem completing the requested action—a firm user should follow up directly and address the specific blocker.

items.q: Can AssurePro send and receive client text messages?
items.a: Yes. AssurePro supports client SMS messaging through a connected Twilio account.
more: After Twilio is connected, the firm can configure a phone number for client texting; Phone Numbers shows which capabilities — SMS, MMS, Voice — each number supports. Firm users can then use SMS from Communications or the client workspace, with replies remaining connected to the client's communication history.
steps: Connect the firm's Twilio account, then open Phone Numbers and link an existing firm-owned number or add a new one.
Confirm the number supports the communication capabilities the firm intends to use.
Complete A2P 10DLC registration for applicable US messaging traffic — unregistered traffic may be filtered or blocked by carriers.
Send a controlled test message to confirm both outbound and inbound messaging work, then begin using SMS for appropriate client communications.

items.q: How do I configure a firm phone number for SMS?
items.a: Firm administrators can configure a phone number for client SMS messaging after connecting the firm's Twilio account.
steps: Open Settings > Integrations and confirm that Twilio is connected.
Open Phone Numbers.
Select Add number.
Choose whether to: Link a phone number already owned in Twilio, Add a new number using the available setup flow.
Review the number under Your numbers and confirm its supported capabilities, such as SMS or MMS.
For applicable U.S. carrier messaging, complete A2P 10DLC registration.
Use Refresh status to confirm the registration result.
Send a controlled test message before using the number for regular client communication.
Before rollout, confirm that the number your firm intends to use is active, supports SMS, and has the required registration status for the type of messaging being sent.

items.q: What phone number does a client see when the firm sends an SMS?
items.a: The client sees the Twilio phone number linked to your firm in AssurePro as the sender of the SMS.
more: If your firm has more than one Twilio number, administrators should confirm which number is linked under Settings > Phone Numbers before telling clients which number to save or recognize. The Phone Numbers area can also show information such as SMS capability, MMS capability, voice capability, and A2P 10DLC registration status.

For U.S. carrier messaging, confirm that the selected number has the required registration status before relying on it for regular client communication — a number may appear in the firm's configuration but still experience carrier filtering if the required messaging registration is incomplete. It is good practice to use a consistent firm number for client SMS so clients can recognize the sender and firm users can maintain a predictable communication channel.

items.q: What calendar connections are supported?
items.a: AssurePro supports calendar and scheduling integrations that help the firm manage client meetings and connect meeting activity to client records.
more: Calendly supports client meeting scheduling; Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar connect calendar activity and can associate a supported meeting with the relevant client record. Connect the provider under Settings > Integrations, then use Calendar for the firm's meeting workflow, and confirm connected meetings are matched to the correct client where matching is available.

items.q: Does everything a client sees carry the firm's branding, or does AssureOne branding appear anywhere?
items.a: AssurePro allows the firm to apply its own branding across key client-facing areas, but some AssureOne branding may still appear in selected platform-managed locations.
more: Firm administrators maintain the firm's core identity in Settings > Firm Profile, including the firm logo, firm name and contact information, primary brand color, and accent color. The client portal address and related portal settings are managed separately under Settings > Client Portal.

The firm's branding is used across supported parts of the client experience, while the AssureOne name may still appear in certain system-managed areas, such as selected email footers or other platform-generated content.

Before rolling AssurePro out to clients, firm administrators should review Firm Profile branding, Client Portal settings and portal address, the client portal experience, Automated Email Templates, desktop and mobile email previews, test emails, and the engagement-letter and document-request experiences. This helps the firm confirm how its branding appears across the client experience and understand where AssureOne platform identification may still be visible.

items.q: How is the Reports area organized?
items.a: The Reports area is organized into three main destinations:
more: Overview provides standard firm KPIs and report cards for a high-level view of firm performance. My Report contains starter dashboards, dashboards shared with the firm, and dashboards created by the signed-in user. Templates provides the report-widget library and tools for building custom dashboards.

Use Overview for a standard firm health check, My Report for dashboards you review regularly, and Templates when you want to create a dashboard with a different combination of metrics. For example, a manager may begin in Overview to review the firm's current billing position, open the Full billing report for more detail, and then duplicate a Billing & Collections dashboard into My dashboards for a customized recurring review.
This structure lets firm users move from high-level monitoring to detailed analysis and then save the views they need for ongoing management.

items.q: Which KPIs appear at the top of Reports?
items.a: The top of Reports includes headline KPI cards that provide a quick view of firm performance.
more: These can include Total Revenue (billed revenue for the selected period), Collected (payments collected during the selected period), Outstanding A/R (client balances that remain unpaid), Billable Hours (time recorded as billable), Utilization (the proportion of available or recorded time used for billable work, based on the firm's reporting setup), and New Clients (clients added during the selected period).

Review these KPIs together rather than in isolation. For example, strong Total Revenue with a growing Outstanding A/R balance may indicate that billing performance is strong but collections require attention.

Before interpreting the KPI cards, select the correct reporting period: MTD (Month to Date), QTD (Quarter to Date), YTD (Year to Date), 12M (Last 12 months), or Custom (a date range selected by the user). Using the same reporting period across the cards helps partners and managers compare the metrics consistently.

items.q: How do I review and export a report?
items.a: Set the reporting period first so the KPI cards, report widgets, detailed dashboards, and exported results reflect the dates you intend to review.
more: AssurePro provides period options such as MTD, QTD, YTD, 12M, and Custom.
steps: Open Reports and choose Overview or My Report.
Select the reporting period: MTD, QTD, YTD, 12M, Custom.
If you choose Custom, enter the required date range.
Review the KPI card, report card, or dashboard that answers your reporting question.
Select Full report where a more detailed view is available.
Review the focused dashboard and its supporting widgets.
Select Export when you need a copy for external analysis, reconciliation, or recordkeeping.
Before exporting, confirm the reporting period and any active filters. This helps ensure the downloaded output matches the same view you reviewed in AssurePro.
For example, if a partner is reviewing year-to-date collections, set the period to YTD before opening the detailed billing report and exporting the results.

items.q: Can report periods and results be changed or exported?
items.a: Yes. AssurePro lets firm users change the reporting period, review more detailed results, and export report data.
more: Available reporting periods include MTD (Month to Date), QTD (Quarter to Date), YTD (Year to Date), 12M (Last 12 months), and Custom (a user-defined date range). Use the period that matches the management question you are reviewing — for example, MTD for current-month operations, QTD for quarterly performance, YTD for year-to-date trends, and Custom for a specific engagement or review period.
Some reports also support additional filters. For example, workflow reporting can be narrowed by stage or by measures such as active and overdue work.

After setting the reporting period and filters, use Full report when a more detailed dashboard is available or Export when you need the results outside AssurePro. Always apply the intended reporting period and filters before opening a detailed report or exporting so the resulting view reflects the correct scope.

items.q: Can report and dashboard data be exported?
items.a: Yes. Firm users can export report and dashboard data for external analysis, reconciliation, or recordkeeping.
steps: Open Reports and choose Overview or My Report.
Select the required reporting period: MTD, QTD, YTD, 12M, or Custom.
Apply any additional filters needed for the review.
Open Full report if you want to export from a focused dashboard rather than the high-level Overview.
Confirm that the visible widgets and filters match the information you need.
Select Export.
Review the exported file before sharing or storing it.

Note: Exported reports may contain client names, financial amounts, workload information, engagement data, or other firm information. Review the file and follow your firm's data-handling and sharing policies before distributing it outside the intended audience.

items.q: What does the agreement funnel report show?
items.a: The Agreement Funnel report shows how engagement-letter signing packages are progressing from delivery through completion.
more: The funnel can track stages and outcomes such as Sent, Viewed, Signed, In progress, Declined, Expired, and Cancelled. Use the funnel to understand where signing packages are moving forward and where they may be getting delayed.

For example, compare Sent to Viewed to identify packages that may not have reached the client's attention, compare Viewed to Signed to identify packages that were opened but have not yet been completed, and review Declined, Expired, or Cancelled packages to understand why they left the active signing process. If a specific package needs follow-up, open the related engagement-letter record to review its recipients, current status, reminder activity, and audit history.
The Agreement Funnel helps partners and managers distinguish a one-off unsigned package from a broader signing bottleneck that may require changes to follow-up, pricing, terms, or onboarding timing.

items.q: What can the AI Agent help with?
items.a: The AssurePro AI Agent can help firm users find, summarize, analyze, and draft information related to client and firm work.
more: It can assist with areas such as clients, documents, engagements and tasks, communications, billing, and deadlines and outstanding work.

Examples of useful requests include "Which engagements have been in the same stage for more than 10 days?", "Summarize unread messages for my assigned clients," "Show clients with outstanding invoices due this month," "Which document requests are still waiting on a client response?", "Summarize work due this week," and "Draft a polite follow-up for overdue invoices, but do not send it."

A good prompt should include the subject (what client, engagement, task, or area you want to review), the time period when relevant, the desired output (summary, list, analysis, or draft), and the action intent (whether you only want information or want the Agent to propose an action). For example, "List my tax engagements due in the next 14 days that still have open document requests, grouped by manager." More specific prompts generally produce more useful results and make it easier for firm users to validate the Agent's response.

items.q: How do I ask the AI Agent for help?
items.a: Ask the AI Agent a specific question in plain language, then review the response, linked records, and any action it proposes.
steps: Open AI Agent.
Enter your question, or choose one of the available suggested prompts.
Include the client, time period, status, or other criteria the question depends on.
Review the Agent's response and any linked records or supporting information.
If the result is too broad, ask a narrower follow-up question.
If the Agent proposes a change, review the action before approving it.
For example, instead of asking: "What needs attention?".
ask: "Show my assigned engagements due in the next seven days that have overdue tasks or missing client documents.".

For actions that can change firm or client data, AssurePro may request confirmation before proceeding. If Auto-approve low-risk actions is enabled for the firm user, supported low-risk actions may proceed without a separate confirmation each time.
Even when an action is proposed by the Agent, firm users should verify important details such as client, recipient, amount, date, engagement, and message content before allowing a change.
If you only want assistance preparing content, make that clear in the prompt—for example, "Draft the message, but do not send it."

items.q: How are AI Agent conversations managed?
items.a: The AI Agent keeps each chat as a separate conversation so firm users can maintain different questions, clients, or work contexts independently.
more: Firm users can start a New chat, reopen a previous conversation from history, rename a conversation, or delete a conversation that is no longer required.
steps: Open AI Agent.
Select New chat when starting a different question, client, or work context.
Enter your request and review the Agent's response, links, sources, and any proposed action.
Use the conversation history to reopen an earlier chat when you need to continue the same context.
Rename important conversations so their purpose is easy to recognize later.
Delete a conversation when it is no longer needed, subject to your firm's information-retention requirements.
For example, a manager may keep separate conversations for Tax Deadline Review, Overdue Billing Follow-up, and Client ABC Engagement Summary instead of mixing unrelated requests in one chat.
Using separate conversations for different clients or management questions helps keep the Agent's context clear and makes prior work easier to find later.

items.q: What is AI Agent memory and how can I control it?
items.a: AI Agent memory is the information the Agent retains for the signed-in firm user so it can use relevant context in future conversations.
