more: Each firm user can control whether memory is enabled and can review or remove saved items.
steps: Open AI Agent > Memory.
Turn memory On when you want the Agent to retain useful context for future conversations.
Turn memory Off when you do not want new context retained beyond the current session.
Select Refresh to review the latest saved memory items.
Use Forget this to remove an individual saved item that should no longer influence future conversations.
Use Clear all memory to remove all saved memory for your user account.
Review saved memory periodically and remove information that is outdated or no longer useful.

Memory is specific to the firm user's AI experience; it should not be treated as a replacement for the official client, engagement, document, billing, or communication records maintained in AssurePro.

items.q: What does Auto-approve low-risk actions do?
items.a: Auto-approve low-risk actions allows the AI Agent to complete supported actions it classifies as low risk without asking the firm user to approve each action individually.
more: When the setting is off, the firm user reviews each proposed change before it is completed. When the setting is on, eligible low-risk actions may proceed automatically, while actions with greater impact still require confirmation. Because the actions classified as low risk may evolve as AI Agent capabilities change, firm users should understand the available behavior and follow the firm's AI and approval policies before enabling this setting.

Leave Auto-approve low-risk actions off when the user should review every proposed change, when the firm requires individual approval for AI-assisted actions, or when the user is still becoming familiar with AI Agent behavior. Enable it only when the firm is comfortable allowing the Agent to complete supported low-risk actions without an additional approval step.
Note: auto-approval of low-risk actions does not authorize higher-impact actions — those actions continue to require confirmation where AssurePro requires it.

items.q: What is the AI-generated daily briefing?
items.a: The AI-generated Daily briefing summarizes recent firm activity and highlights items that may need attention, using the firm's current AssurePro data for the selected period rather than a fixed set of sample metrics.
more: Depending on recent activity, it may summarize overdue invoices, payments received, completed tasks, workflow-stage changes, engagements requiring attention, document uploads, client messages, or newly added clients.

For example, if the briefing reports four overdue invoices, a manager can select the related source records, review which clients and balances are affected, open Billing to confirm invoice status and due dates, and check whether payment or follow-up has already occurred.
steps: Open Overview and choose Today, This week, or This month to set the period the briefing covers.
Review each insight for its activity, count, and potential impact.
Select View sources to review the records behind an insight, or use the available Next actions to open the relevant area of AssurePro.

Use the connected Overview tiles for further follow-up — Billing for invoices, Clients for client records, Engagements or Bottlenecks for Workflow, Team load for capacity, Documents for document work, Communications for client follow-up.
Select Re-Generate when the underlying activity has changed and a fresh briefing is needed.

items.q: What use is tracked in AI Credits?
items.a: AI Credits track usage of AI-powered features across AssureOne so the firm can see where credits are being consumed.
more: Credits may be used by AI Agent interactions, summaries, draft generation, call transcription, document reading and extraction, and product-specific AI assistance in AssurePro, AssureTax, AssureAudit, or AssureBooks. The AI Credits page shows both the remaining balance and detailed usage activity — activity, feature, firm user, product, date, and credits consumed for each entry — so administrators can identify what is driving consumption. Invoices or receipts for purchased credits are available under Settings > Platform Subscription.
steps: Open Settings > AI Credits and review Available credits and usage for the last 30 days.
Filter by product — All products, Pro, Tax, Audit, or Books — and by All team members or an individual firm user.
Review each usage entry's activity, feature, firm user, product, date, and credits consumed; use About when more context is available.

items.q: How much do AI Credits cost, and how are more credits purchased?
items.a: Firm administrators can purchase additional AI Credits from Settings > AI Credits when the available balance needs topping up.
more: The purchase screen currently offers $25 for 2,500 credits, $50 for 5,000 credits, $100 for 10,000 credits, or a custom amount. Credits are billed at the underlying AI usage cost without a markup, and the firm decides when to buy more. Payment is handled through the payment experience secured by Stripe, and the related invoice or receipt is available under Settings > Platform Subscription.
steps: Open Settings > AI Credits and review the current balance and recent usage.
Select Buy credits, choose a predefined pack or enter a custom amount, and review the purchase amount, credits added, and payment method.
Confirm the purchase; the additional credits are added to the firm's balance.

items.q: Are AI Credits replenished automatically or included as a monthly allowance?
items.a: No. AI Credits are not automatically added back, and they do not reset to a set amount each month.
more: Your firm controls when additional credits are purchased. AssurePro does not automatically charge the firm's payment method when the balance becomes low or reaches zero. Firm administrators can monitor the remaining credit balance, review recent AI usage, and purchase a predefined credit pack or a custom top-up amount.

As a planning reference, a firm with approximately five to ten users using AssurePro together with one additional AssureOne product may use around $50 of AI Credits per month under typical usage. Actual consumption can vary based on factors such as document volume, AI Agent usage, summarization, drafting, extraction, transcription, and other AI-powered activity.
Use the firm's actual usage history in Settings > AI Credits as the primary basis for future credit planning.

items.q: What happens when the firm runs out of AI Credits?
items.a: The firm's remaining AI Credit balance is visible in the application header and under Settings > AI Credits. When the balance reaches zero, features that require AI Credits pause until more are purchased — AssurePro does not automatically charge the firm's card or replenish the balance.
more: For example, if the balance reaches zero during document extraction, drafting, or summarization, add credits first and then restart the action rather than assuming the original request completed. To reduce interruptions, monitor both Available credits and last-30-days usage so credits can be purchased before the balance runs out.
steps: Open Settings > AI Credits and review the current balance and recent usage.
Select Buy credits, choose a pack or enter a custom amount, and complete the purchase.
Confirm the new credits appear in the available balance, then restart the AI-powered activity that was interrupted.

items.q: How can administrators control AI Credit usage across the firm?
items.a: Firm administrators can monitor and manage AI Credit consumption from Settings > AI Credits.
more: The AI Credits area provides visibility into usage across AssurePro, AssureTax, AssureAudit, and AssureBooks, broken down by individual firm users, AI features and activities, and dates and credits consumed. Administrators can also manage how credits are distributed across the team by assigning user-level allocations or usage caps where available.

For example, an administrator may allocate more credits to a firm user who regularly performs AI-assisted document or client work, set a lower usage cap for a user who only needs occasional AI assistance, compare usage across Pro, Tax, Audit, and Books, review individual usage when the firm's overall consumption increases unexpectedly, and adjust allocations as responsibilities or workloads change. These controls help the firm manage AI usage without disabling approved AI functionality for the entire practice.

Because AssureOne does not automatically replenish the balance or charge the firm's card, administrators should review usage trends, user allocations, and remaining credits together when deciding when to purchase additional credits and how much to add.

items.q: Are AI Credits shared across the firm, or can they be allocated by firm user?
items.a: AI Credits are purchased at the firm level, and firm administrators can manage how that balance is allocated across individual firm users.
more: Administrators can review AI Credit usage by AssureOne product, review usage by individual firm user, allocate credits to firm users, set per-user usage caps, and adjust allocations as responsibilities or usage patterns change.

For example, if the firm purchases 10,000 credits, an administrator can allocate a larger portion to users who regularly use AI-assisted document review, drafting, or analysis, while setting lower limits for users who only need occasional AI assistance. The Credit Usage section shows where credits have been consumed, allowing administrators to make allocation decisions based on actual usage rather than estimates.
Review allocations periodically, especially when team responsibilities, workloads, or use of AssurePro, AssureTax, AssureAudit, or AssureBooks changes.

items.q: Can we control what data the AI Agent retains?
items.a: Yes. Each firm user can control the context retained by the AI Agent through AI Agent > Memory.
more: Firm users can turn Memory on when useful context should be retained for future conversations, turn it off when new context should not be retained beyond the current session, review the items currently saved in memory, use Forget this to remove an individual saved item, and use Clear all memory to remove all saved Agent memory for that user.

For example, a firm user may retain a stable working preference that is useful across conversations while removing temporary client-specific context once it is no longer needed. Review saved memory periodically so retained information remains relevant and appropriate.

Note: AI Agent memory is contextual assistance for future AI conversations. It should not be used as the system of record for client information, engagement details, documents, billing, or other firm records maintained elsewhere in AssurePro.

items.q: Can an AI Agent action be undone, and is there an audit trail of what it did?
items.a: AssurePro does not provide one universal Undo action for every change completed by the AI Agent.
more: Before approving an Agent-proposed action, firm users should review the affected information carefully, including the client or record, recipient, amount, date, engagement or task, and proposed change. If your firm requires users to review every AI-assisted change before it occurs, leave Auto-approve low-risk actions turned off.

If an AI Agent action needs to be corrected, open the affected area of AssurePro and use the available edit, update, or reversal controls for that specific record, where supported. For auditability, Settings > AI Credits shows AI usage and attribution, such as the feature used, firm user, product, date, and credits consumed — however, AI Credit usage should not be treated as a complete audit log of every data change performed by the Agent. Where available, use the affected record's own activity history, audit trail, status history, or other record-level history to review what happened.

A useful distinction is that AI Credits show who used AI and where credits were consumed, while record activity or audit history shows what happened to the underlying client or firm record. For higher-impact actions, firm users should validate the proposed change before approval rather than relying on the ability to undo it later.

items.q: Do unused AI Credits expire or roll over?
items.a: No. Unused AI Credits do not expire and do not reset at the end of a month or subscription cycle.
more: Any unused balance remains available to the firm until the credits are consumed. There is no monthly rollover calculation because the credits simply stay in the firm's available balance.
For example, if your firm purchases 5,000 credits and uses 3,500 credits, the remaining 1,500 credits remain available for future AI-powered activity.
Because credits do not expire, administrators can purchase based on expected usage rather than trying to use the balance before a renewal date.
Review Available credits and recent usage in Settings > AI Credits to decide when an additional purchase is actually needed.

items.q: Which third-party services can be connected?
items.a: AssurePro supports third-party integrations for email, meetings, document storage, client payments, accounting, SMS, and other connected workflows.
more: Available integrations include Gmail and Outlook for firm email, Calendly for meeting scheduling, Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar for calendar and meeting activity, Dropbox and OneDrive for document storage and import, Twilio for client SMS, the payment processor shown in Integrations for online client payments, QuickBooks Online for accounting synchronization, and ProdAff for the ProdAff connection shown in Integrations.

Firm administrators can review and manage available providers under Settings > Integrations. The integration you choose depends on the workflow your firm wants to support — for example, connect Dropbox or OneDrive for cloud document import, Twilio for client SMS, and QuickBooks Online when paid-invoice information should flow into the firm's accounting process.

items.q: How do I connect and test an integration?
items.a: Firm administrators can connect supported external services from Settings > Integrations.
more: Where possible, use a firm-controlled provider account rather than an individual user's temporary or personal account, particularly for integrations that support firm-wide workflows.
steps: Open Settings > Integrations.
Find the provider your firm wants to use.
Select Connect.
Complete the provider's authorization process.
Return to AssurePro and confirm that the provider shows as Connected.
Confirm that the connected account or identity is the one your firm intended to authorize.
Test the specific workflow that depends on the integration.
For example:
Send an internal test email after connecting Gmail or Outlook.
Import a non-sensitive test file after connecting Dropbox or OneDrive.
Create or verify a test meeting after connecting a calendar provider.
Send and receive a test SMS after connecting Twilio.
Complete a controlled payment or accounting test before relying on a financial integration.
A Connected status confirms that authorization has been established. A successful end-to-end test confirms that the integration is usable for your firm's workflow.

items.q: Which AssurePro workflows depend on a connected service?
items.a: Some AssurePro features require a third-party service to be connected before the workflow can be used.
more: Examples include email communication (Gmail or Outlook), client SMS (Twilio and a configured firm phone number), meeting scheduling (Calendly), calendar and meeting association (Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar), cloud document import (Dropbox or OneDrive), online client payments (the configured payment processor), and paid-invoice accounting synchronization (QuickBooks Online).

For example, if Dropbox or OneDrive is not connected, cloud document import cannot proceed. SMS requires both a connected Twilio account and a linked phone number, while online invoice payment depends on the firm's payment-processor configuration.

Because a disconnected or expired authorization can affect multiple users, the firm should also maintain clear ownership of each integration and periodically confirm that critical connections remain active.

items.q: What is the Tax Connector?
items.a: The Tax Connector is used to approve Windows computers that import supported tax-software data into AssureTax.
more: Each computer is paired individually and receives its own import-only credential after approval. The Tax Connector setup includes a pairing code with a 10-minute validity period, individual approval for each Windows computer, a revocable import-only credential, connected-computer status, last-seen information, credential-expiration information, and platform and application-version details.
steps: Open Settings > Tax Connector.
Enter the pairing code displayed by the Tax Connector within the 10-minute validity window.
Select Approve computer if you recognize the request.
Select Deny if the request is unexpected or unrecognized.
Review approved devices under Connected computers.
Use Revoke when a computer should no longer be allowed to import data.
Revocation takes effect when the connector next attempts to communicate with AssureOne.
Review the connected-computer list periodically and revoke devices that are no longer used by the firm.

items.q: How are shared firm and client credentials handled?
items.a: AssurePro keeps firm-wide credentials and client-specific credentials in separate areas.
more: Firm Credentials is used for shared internal logins that apply across the practice.
The client Credentials tab is used for login information that belongs to a specific client.
Stored credentials are protected with encryption at rest, and access to reveal sensitive values is controlled through permissions and engagement ownership.
AssurePro also records credential-reveal activity so access can be reviewed at any time.
steps: Open Settings > Firm Credentials for a firm-wide credential, or open the client's Credentials tab for a client-specific login.
Select Add your first credential or Add credential.
Enter the service and credential information.
Confirm that access is limited to the appropriate firm users.
Use the available reveal-history information when credential access needs to be reviewed.

Keep client credentials in the client workspace rather than placing them in the firm-wide credential store. This helps maintain the correct relationship between the credential and the client it belongs to.

items.q: What can firm users manage in Security settings?
items.a: The Security settings currently allow the signed-in firm user to change their AssurePro password.
more: Changing the password affects only that user's own account. It does not change team membership, roles or permissions, product access, client portal credentials, or other firm users' passwords.
steps: Open Settings > Security.
Enter the Current Password.
Enter the new password.
Confirm the new password.
Select Change Password.
The new password must meet the minimum password requirements shown in AssurePro.
Use a unique password that also complies with your firm's internal security policy, and store it in an approved password manager.

items.q: How is account access managed for firm users and client users?
items.a: Firm-user access and client-user access are managed separately in AssurePro.
more: A firm user manages their own password under Settings > Security. Firm administrators manage broader access — team membership, roles, permissions, product access, and account status — under Team & Roles. Client access is managed from the client record: firm users can manage the client contact's portal invitation, email address, portal-access status, and invitation resend.
This separation is deliberate: changing a firm user's role does not affect a client's portal access, and changing a client contact does not change any firm user's permissions.

items.q: How are notifications and report alerts controlled?
items.a: Firm users can control personal notifications under Settings > Notifications & Email, while report alerts can be configured for firm-level KPI monitoring.
more: Personal notifications: firm users can independently enable or disable email and in-app notifications for new document uploads, client messages, invoice payments, upcoming deadlines, and overdue invoices — for example, enabling both channels for overdue invoices while using only in-app for routine uploads.

Report alerts: notify selected firm users when a KPI reaches a defined threshold, or send a scheduled digest of selected firm metrics. Use threshold alerts for conditions needing timely action, such as rising A/R or workflow backlog, and scheduled digests for recurring management reviews.

items.q: Where is firm and client data hosted, and is it encrypted?
items.a: AssurePro runs on Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure.
more: Firm and client data is protected using encryption both in transit and at rest. For stored credentials, AssurePro states that Firm Credentials and client Credentials use AES-256 encryption at rest — reveal access is controlled through permissions and engagement ownership, and credential-reveal activity is logged.

Firms completing a security or vendor-risk review should request the latest AssureOne security documentation for details such as hosting architecture, data location, backup approach, retention, encryption, disaster recovery, and security controls.
Because infrastructure and security controls can evolve, use the current AssureOne security documentation rather than relying only on knowledge-base summaries for formal due diligence.

items.q: Does AssurePro hold compliance certifications such as SOC 2?
items.a: Security certifications, audit reports, and their coverage can change over time.
more: If your firm is completing vendor due diligence, request the current AssureOne security and compliance package and verify the exact certification or report status before relying on it. The review should confirm items such as the certification or report name, services and products covered, audit period, current validity period, subservice organizations, customer responsibilities, and any bridge letter covering the period since the last audit.

A bridge letter may be relevant when the most recent audit period does not extend through the date of your firm's security review. Your firm's security, compliance, or risk lead should review the current documentation directly.
Do not treat language such as planned, in progress, or coming soon as evidence that a certification is already active.

items.q: Is multi-factor authentication available for firm users and client users?
items.a: AssurePro currently uses a one-time email verification step during account activation for both firm users and client users.
more: During activation, the user opens the invitation sent to their email address, verifies the invited email address using the verification step provided, creates a password, and uses those credentials for future sign-in. This activation verification confirms that the user has access to the invited mailbox — it is not the same as recurring multi-factor authentication at every sign-in.

If a verification code or invitation does not arrive, for a firm user, confirm the email under Team & Roles > Invitations and resend the invitation if needed; for a client user, confirm the contact email on the client Info tab and resend the portal invitation. Ask the recipient to check spam or email-filtering folders before resending.
Verification codes should not be forwarded between users because they are intended to confirm access to the specific mailbox that received the invitation.

items.q: Can the firm export its data if it cancels its AssurePro subscription?
items.a: Yes, but the data-export and account-closure process should be planned with the AssureOne account team before access is terminated.
more: The firm and AssureOne team should confirm the records that need to be retained, the documents that need to be exported, available export formats, the required historical period, export method, account-closure date, and validation responsibilities. Before the account is closed, download and review the agreed exports.

A practical offboarding checklist can include exporting client and contact records, exporting open and historical engagement information where required, downloading required client documents, exporting billing and invoice records, exporting communication records where available and required, confirming that files open correctly, reconciling record counts against AssurePro, and storing the exported information in the firm's approved retention location.

For example, compare the number of exported clients, active engagements, invoices, and documents with the totals visible in AssurePro before access ends. Keep the account active until the firm has confirmed that the required data has been exported, validated, and stored successfully.
